what: -reportNotSpamMessages:inChat:completion: sends the TDLib method that does the exact opposite of what the header promises: `[self cm_toggleSupergroup:@"reportSupergroupSpam" chat:chatId fields:@{@"message_ids" : messageIds ?: @[]} completion:completion];`

A user who taps a 'not spam' affordance would report the innocent messages as spam to Telegram, and the call returns ok:YES so the UI confirms success. The method has no callers today, so this is a live trap for the next screen that wires it up rather than a bug the user can hit right now.

what: -markForumTopicReadInChat:topic:completion: only sends readAllForumTopicMentions, readAllForumTopicReactions and readAllForumTopicPollVotes; it never marks the topic's messages read (no viewMessages / force_read).
failure: TGTopicsViewController.m:1197 wires this to the row action whose key is "read" and whose failure text is "Could not mark the topic as read."; TGTopicsViewController.m:1037 also calls it when a topic is opened. Tapping 'Mark as read' repeatedly never clears the badge.

what: TGCMEventFilterFields() lists only 13 of the 15 chatEventLogFilters booleans - `member_tag_changes` and `subscription_extensions` are missing from the map, and -eventLogForChat: builds the filter object from that map alone (line 1047: `for (NSString *key in fields) filter[fields[key]] = @(!filters || [filters containsObject:key]);`).

Concretely: an admin changes another admin's custom title (a member_tag_change) and TGChatEventsViewController's Recent Actions list never shows that row, with no way for the user to turn it on.

what: -myRightsInChat:completion: reads a field that does not exist in this TDLib schema: `NSString *title = TGCMString(status[@"custom_title"]);` where `status` is a ChatMemberStatus object.
failure: td_api.tl:2475-2492 defines chatMemberStatusCreator/Administrator/Member/Restricted with no custom_title member at all - this schema carries the title on `chatMember.tag` (td_api.tl:2508) instead. Any screen that renders it shows nothing where the group owner's title ("Founder", etc.) should appear.

what: -setSlowModeDelay:forChat: snaps downward, not to the nearest preset: `for (NSNumber *preset in [TGClient slowModePresets]) { if ([preset integerValue] <= seconds) allowed = [preset integerValue]; }`
failure: TGClient+ChatManagement.h:120 says the value is rounded to "the nearest allowed value". With presets @[0,10,30,60,300,900,3600], a caller asking for 800 seconds gets 300 (nearest is 900), 250 gets 60 (nearest is 300), and anything under 10 silently disables slow mode entirely. A caller that computes a delay rather than picking from -slowModePresets sets a far weaker restriction than requested and gets ok:YES.
fix: Replace the loop with a nearest-value search: track the preset minimising llabs(preset - seconds), breaking ties toward the larger preset; or change the header text at TGClient+ChatManagement.h:120 to say the value is rounded down to the next allowed preset.

what: TGClient+Groups.m (1447 lines) is a second, largely unused implementation of TGClient+ChatManagement.m (1107 lines). Both categories implement the same TDLib calls with different helper names (TGDict/TGArray/TGString/TGIsError vs TGCMDict/TGCMArray/TGCMString/TGCMFailed; TGPermissionKeys vs TGCMPermissionFields; TGAdminRightKeys vs TGCMRightFields; tg_group: vs cm_supergroupForChat:; tg_supergroupToggle: vs cm_toggleSupergroup:; tg_link: vs cm_requestLink:; TGFlattenInviteLink vs TGCMFlatInviteLink) and different output key vocabularies (snake_case TDLib names in Groups, camelCase in ChatManagement).
failure: 40 of TGClient+Groups.h's public methods have no caller anywhere in src/ - the entire invite-link stack (primaryInviteLinkForGroup:, replacePrimaryInviteLinkForGroup:, createInviteLinkInGroup:..., inviteLinksInGroup:..., inviteLinkCountsInGroup:), the entire join-request stack (joinRequestsInGroup:limit:, processAllJoinRequestsInGroup:), all of createBasicGroupWithTitle:/createSupergroupWithTitle:/upgradeBasicGroupToSupergroup:, setGroupChat:title:/description:/photoAtPath:/username:, every setGroup:* switch, eventLogForGroup:, reportGroup:, suitableDiscussionGroupsWithCompletion:, createdPublicChatsWithCompletion:. TGInviteLinksViewController uses the ChatManagement versions exclusively. The cost is ~700 lines of armv7 code and its literal dictionaries resident in a 512MB device, plus the standing hazard that the two key vocabularies get crossed: a dictionary from -defaultPermissionsInGroup: (keys "can_send_basic_messages", ...) passed to -setPermissions:forChat: (reads keys "sendMessages", ...) would send an all-false chatPermissions and silently mute the whole group.
fix: Delete from TGClient+Groups.{h,m} the 40 unreferenced methods listed by the caller scan, and with them the now-orphaned TGFlattenInviteLink and tg_link:completion: helpers. Keep the 20 methods TGGroupMembersViewController/TGProfileViewController actually call (groupInfoForChat:, membersInGroup:..., searchMembersInGroup:..., memberStatusOfUser:..., administratorRightsOfUser:..., permissionsOfUser:..., myAdministratorRightsInGroup:, defaultPermissionsInGroup:, promoteMember:..., restrictMember:..., banMember:..., removeMember:..., unbanMember:..., deleteAllMessagesFromUser:..., administratorRightKeys, memberPermissionKeys, titleFor*Key:). Do not merge the two key vocabularies in the same pass - each surviving method's callers depend on its current spelling.

what: -setOnFoldersChanged: copies its block into a file-static that is never cleared: `static void (^TGFoldersChangedBlock)(void) = nil;` (line 68) / `TGFoldersChangedBlock = [block copy];` (line 932). Neither -setOnFoldersChanged: nor its getter -onFoldersChanged has a caller anywhere in src/.
failure: Dead today; a leak the moment it is used. A view controller calling `[client setOnFoldersChanged:^{ [self reload]; }]` captures self strongly into a process-lifetime static, so the controller and its whole view hierarchy are never deallocated even after being popped - on a 40-60MB budget that is a permanent tens-of-KB-per-visit leak. TGFoldersViewController.m:137 already uses the NSNotificationCenter path (TGChatFoldersDidChangeNotification), which is the correct one.
fix: Delete -setOnFoldersChanged:, -onFoldersChanged, the TGFoldersChangedBlock static (line 68) and its invocation at line 97-98 from TGClient+ChatList.m, plus their declarations in TGClient+ChatList.h. -beginObservingFolderChanges and the notification stay.

what: -joinGroupByInviteLink:completion: branches on a result type this schema never produces and silently swallows two it does: `else if ([type isEqualToString:@"chat"]) completion([result[@"id"] longLongValue], NO); else completion(0, NO);`
failure: td_api.tl:13965 declares `joinChatByInviteLink invite_link:string = ChatJoinResult;` with exactly four cases (chatJoinResultSuccess, chatJoinResultRequestSent, chatJoinResultGuardBotApprovalRequired, chatJoinResultDeclined). The @"chat" branch is unreachable dead code left over from an older schema, while chatJoinResultDeclined and chatJoinResultGuardBotApprovalRequired both fall into the final `completion(0, NO)`, which is byte-identical to a network error. A user whose join was declined by the group's guard bot gets the generic failure message instead of the real reason. The same shape exists in TGClient+ChatManagement.m:867-872 (which has no chatJoinResultSuccess branch at all and instead reads result[@"chat_id"] unconditionally, giving 0 for the two unhandled cases).

what: -setGroup:slowModeDelay:completion: forwards the caller's seconds straight through with no validation: `@"slow_mode_delay" : @(seconds)`, unlike -setSlowModeDelay:forChat: in TGClient+ChatManagement.m:385 which snaps to a preset.
failure: TDLib rejects setChatSlowModeDelay for any value outside {0,10,30,60,300,900,3600} with an error, so this method answers NO for e.g. 45 seconds while the ChatManagement twin answers YES having quietly applied 30. Two APIs on the same class disagree about the contract for the same TDLib call. Currently dead (no callers), so the disagreement is latent.
fix: Delete -setGroup:slowModeDelay:completion: as part of the TGClient+Groups dead-code removal above; -setSlowModeDelay:forChat:completion: is the surviving API.

what: TGChatTitleCache() is a process-lifetime NSMutableDictionary with no eviction, written on every chat-list render: `if ([row[@"title"] isKindOfClass:NSString.class] && [row[@"title"] length] > 0) TGChatTitleCache()[chatId] = row[@"title"];` inside -tgcl_rowsForChatIds:, plus writes at lines 858 and 890. TGMarkedUnreadChatIds() (line 54) is the same pattern.
failure: Every chat id the user ever scrolls past, searches for, or gets a title lookup on keeps an NSNumber key and an NSString title alive until the process dies; searchPublicChats results count too, so global search over many queries grows it without bound. On the 4S's ~40-60MB budget this is tens of KB after heavy use rather than a crash, but it is unbounded and it duplicates data self.chatsById already holds (the cache exists only to survive chatsById evictions).
fix: Cap it: in -tgcl_rowsForChatIds: skip the cache write when self.chatsById already holds the title (it always does at that point - the row came from chatsById), which removes the search-result growth entirely; or replace both statics with an NSCache with countLimit 200 and drop them in -didReceiveMemoryWarning / -logOut.

what: premiumSubscriptionWithCompletion: reads a premium expiry that TDLib never sends: `long long expires = [TGPremiumNumber(state[@"expiration_date"]) longLongValue]; if (!expires) expires = [TGPremiumNumber(text[@"expiration_date"]) longLongValue];`
failure: td_api.tl:8166 defines `premiumState state:formattedText payment_options:vector<premiumStatePaymentOption> animations:... business_animations:...`. There is no `expiration_date` on premiumState and none on its `state` (a formattedText, fields `text`/`entities`). Both lookups always miss, `expires` is always 0, so the `expires > 0` branch at line 219 is unreachable and `expiresText` is always the literal "Active". TGPremiumViewController.m:143-146 shows `expiresText` as the subscription subtitle, so a subscriber's Premium screen can never display the renewal date. The identical dead lookup exists a second time in TGClient.m:1481 (`state[@"state"][@"expiration_date"] ?: state[@"expiration_date"]`).

Delete lines 213-217 and the `@"expires"` output key, and set expiresText from `active` alone ("Active"), or obtain the date elsewhere (e.g. cache `subscription_until_date` from the messagePaymentSuccessful service message in chat 777000) before claiming to show one. Apply the same removal to TGClient.m:1481 so the two copies do not drift again.

what: `@"queryId" : TGBNumber(result[@"inline_query_id"])` treats an int64 td_api field as an NSNumber.
failure: tdlib/td/td/tl/tl_json.h:29-31 serializes every td_api `int64` through `JsonInt64`, which writes `jv << JsonString(...)` - i.e. int64 fields arrive as JSON *strings*, unlike int53 (chat/user/message ids) which arrive as numbers. td_api.tl:7614 declares `inlineQueryResults inline_query_id:int64 ...`, so `result[@"inline_query_id"]` is an NSString, `TGBNumber` fails its isKindOfClass check and returns @0. The dictionary handed to the UI carries queryId 0, and -sendInlineResult:queryId:toChat:replyTo:hideVia: (line 587, `@"query_id" : queryId ?: @0`) then sends `query_id: 0`, so every attempt to send an inline-bot result fails with a TDLib "Wrong query_id" error and nothing is sent.
fix: At line 578 use the string form: `@"queryId" : TGBString(result[@"inline_query_id"])`, and in -sendInlineResult:... pass that string straight through as `@"query_id"` (TDLib's from_json for int64 accepts String as well as Number, tl_json.h:91-101). Change the `queryId:(NSNumber *)` parameter in TGClient+Bots.h to `(NSString *)` to match.

what: `@"id" : TGPremiumNumber(giveaway[@"id"])` in the prepaid-giveaway loop of -chatBoostStatusForChat:completion:.
failure: td_api.tl:6828 declares `prepaidGiveaway id:int64 winner_count:int32 prize:GiveawayPrize boost_count:int32 payment_date:int32`, and int64 is serialized as a JSON string (tl_json.h:29). `TGPremiumNumber` therefore returns @0 for every prepaid giveaway. A caller that feeds that `id` into -launchPrepaidGiveaway:inChat:... (line 625) sends `giveaway_id: 0`, and TDLib rejects the launch with "Giveaway not found" - the prepaid giveaway can never be started from this client.
fix: At line 697 emit the raw string: `@"id" : TGPremiumString(giveaway[@"id"])`, and change -launchPrepaidGiveaway: to take an NSString giveawayId and put it into the request unchanged (TDLib accepts String for int64). Same treatment for any other int64 field read through TGPremiumNumber.

what: -instantViewForUrl:completion: can invoke its completion twice: `if (blocks.count && completion) completion(cached);` at line 876-877, then `completion(fresh)` at line 886 when the cached copy was not full.
failure: A cached-but-partial instant view (blocks present, `is_full` false - the normal case for a first local hit) fires the completion once with the cached page and a second time with the network page. The only caller, TGInstantViewController (TGChatViewController.m:356), responds by calling -adoptBlocks: each time, which spawns a second global-queue layout pass over every block while the first is still running and then reassigns `_blocks`/`_heights` and reloads the table. On a single-core A5 the two passes contend, and because each pass publishes `_blocks` and `_heights` from its own async block, the table can be reloaded with the heights of one page and the blocks of the other (rows drawn at the wrong height, content clipped). Callers written against the header, which documents a single callback, have no way to know a second one is coming.
fix: Either make the method single-shot - drop the early `completion(cached)` at 876-877 and always deliver the result of the onlyLocal:NO pass, falling back to `cached` when `fresh` is nil - or rename it to a two-phase API (e.g. -instantViewForUrl:progress:completion:) and update TGInstantViewController to cancel/ignore a stale -adoptBlocks: pass by tagging each pass with a generation counter.

what: The premium gift-code and gift-premium API is implemented twice, in two categories on TGClient, with different result shapes: -checkPremiumGiftCode:completion: (Payments.m:1354) vs -checkGiftCode:completion: (Premium.m:447); -applyPremiumGiftCode:completion: (Payments.m:1379) vs -applyGiftCode:completion: (Premium.m:484); -giftPremiumWithStarsToUser:starCount:months:text:completion: (Payments.m:1385) vs -giftPremiumToUser:months:stars:message:completion: (Premium.m:525).
failure: The two check-code flatteners disagree about the same TDLib object: Premium emits keys `months`/`days`/`used`/`creatorIsChat`, Payments emits `monthCount`/`dayCount`/`useDate` and no `used` flag, and Payments' `creatorId` (line 1366, `creator[@"user_id"] ?: creator[@"chat_id"]`) silently mixes user ids and chat ids into one key with no discriminator, so a giveaway created by a channel resolves as a user id. Only the Premium variants are reachable (TGPremiumViewController.m:607 -> -redeemGiftCode:); the Payments trio is never called from any screen. Anyone who wires a new screen to the Payments version gets a dictionary the existing gift-code UI cannot read.
fix: Delete -checkPremiumGiftCode:completion:, -applyPremiumGiftCode:completion: and -giftPremiumWithStarsToUser:starCount:months:text:completion: from TGClient+Payments.m/.h (lines 1354-1400) and keep the TGClient+Premium.m versions as the single entry point.

what: getStarTransactions is wrapped twice with incompatible output: -starTransactionsWithOffset:limit:completion: (Premium.m:1166, keys `refund`/`type`/`title`, returns a dictionary with `balance`) and -starTransactionsWithDirection:offset:limit:completion: (Payments.m:316 + -tg_flattenTransaction: at 271, keys `isRefund`/`userId`/`chatId`/`photoFileId`, returns array+offset).
failure: Only the Premium wrapper is used (TGStarsViewController.m:264), and it never writes the module-static balance cache `TGPayCachedStarBalance` (Payments.m:92) that the same screen reads through -cachedStarBalance at TGStarsViewController.m:262. Paging the star history therefore never warms the cache, so every fresh entry into the Stars screen starts with `self.balance = 0` and `balanceKnown = NO` until a full transaction request completes - the balance row flickers from unknown to a value on every push, even though the value was already fetched a second earlier.
fix: Keep one implementation. Simplest: in TGClient+Premium.m:1203-1205, after computing `balance`, also publish it - move the cache into TGClient+Private.h (or expose a `-setCachedStarBalance:`) and set it there; then delete -starTransactionsWithDirection:offset:limit:completion: and -tg_flattenTransaction: from Payments.m unless a caller for the direction filter is added.

what: The entire TGClient (Bots) category - 734 lines, keyboards, callback buttons, inline queries, bot info, write-access - is unreachable.
failure: No file outside TGClient+Bots.m imports TGClient+Bots.h, and no selector it defines (-inlineKeyboardRowsForMessage:, -replyKeyboardForMessage:, -pressCallbackButton:inChat:message:completion:, -inlineQueryToBot:..., -sendInlineResult:..., -botInfoForUser:..., -shareUsersWithBot..., -viaBotForMessage:..., -botServiceTextForMessage:) appears in any other .m. `reply_markup` is not read anywhere in the UI layer. -getCallbackQueryAnswer is additionally implemented a second time as -pressInlineButtonWithData:onMessage:inChat:completion: (TGClient+Messages.m:983), which is also uncalled. The cost is not only ~734 dead lines: the category is compiled and its +load-time method list is attached to TGClient at every launch, and the bugs inside it (see the inline_query_id finding) are invisible because nothing exercises them.
fix: Decide the owner before wiring any bot UI: keep TGClient+Bots.m as the single bot layer and delete -pressInlineButtonWithData:onMessage:inChat:completion: from TGClient+Messages.m:983-1009 plus its header declaration, or drop TGClient+Bots.{h,m} from the Makefile source list entirely. Do not leave both.

what: Large unreferenced blocks in Payments and WebLinks: the whole payment-form/receipt path (Payments.m:361-691: -tg_paymentFormForInvoice:, -paymentFormForMessage:inChat:, -paymentFormForInvoiceName:, -tg_sendPaymentForm:..., -payStarsPaymentForm:, -unlockPaidMediaInMessage:..., -validateOrderInfo:..., -payCardPaymentForm:..., -paymentReceiptForMessage:..., -clearSavedPaymentInfoWithCompletion:), the gift catalogue/collections/resale path (Payments.m:695-1233), and in WebLinks +flattenedLinkPreview:, +tappableEntitiesIn:, +linkPreviewOptionsDisabled:..., -linkForInternalType:isHttp:completion:, -publicLinkForUsername:, -publicLinkForStickerSetName:, -loginUrlInfoForButton:..., -loginUrlForButton:..., -deepLinkInfoForUrl:..., -applicationDownloadLinkWithCompletion:.

(TGReactionPickerView.m), -receivedGiftsFor... and -cachedStarBalance (TGStarsViewController.m); the only live WebLinks entry points are -resolveLink:completion:, -externalLinkInfoForUrl:completion:, -externalLinkForUrl:allowWriteAccess:completion: (TGChatViewController.m), -recentlyVisitedTMeUrlsWithReferrer:completion: (TGSearchViewController.m) and -instantViewForUrl:completion:. what: `NSString *senderName = senderId ? [self nameForUserId:[senderId longLongValue]] : nil;` where `senderId` came from `sender[@"user_id"] ?: sender[@"chat_id"]` (line 803).
failure: receivedGift.sender_id is a MessageSender (td_api.tl:1787), so a gift sent by a channel yields messageSenderChat and `senderId` is a negative chat id. -nameForUserId: looks that id up in usersById (TGClient.m:2226), which only holds user ids, so it returns nil and `senderName` becomes "". Gifts received from channels display with a blank sender in the Stars screen, and the `senderId` key gives the consumer no way to tell a user id from a chat id.
fix: Mirror what Premium.m:463-466 does: record `BOOL isChat = [TGPayString(sender[@"@type"]) isEqualToString:@"messageSenderChat"]`, put it in the output under `senderIsChat`, and resolve the name via `[self nameForUserId:...]` for users and `TGPayString([self.chatsById[senderId] objectForKey:@"title"])` for chats (the pattern already used at Payments.m:1340-1341).

what: `NSDictionary *link = TGPremiumDict(option[@"payment_link"]); ... @"link" : TGPremiumString(link[@"url"])`
failure: td_api.tl:1356 declares `premiumPaymentOption ... payment_link:InternalLinkType`, and the variants TDLib actually returns here (internalLinkTypePremiumFeaturesPage:9450 `referrer:string`, internalLinkTypePremiumGiftPurchase:9459, internalLinkTypeUnknownDeepLink:9528 `link:string`) have no `url` field. The `link` key of every payment option is therefore always the empty string, so any purchase button wired to it would open nothing.
fix: Store the raw link object instead of a fabricated url: `@"paymentLink" : link ?: @{}`, and resolve it with -linkForInternalType:isHttp:completion: (TGClient+WebLinks.m:471) when the option is tapped. If nothing will consume it, drop the key.

what: chatsToPostStoriesWithCompletion: resolves the title of every chat id with -nameForUserId:, which is only a lookup in usersById: `NSString *title = [weakSelf nameForUserId:chatId.longLongValue] ?: @"";`
failure: getChatsToPostStories returns the user's own chat id plus the ids of channels the user administers. Channel ids are negative (-100...) and are never keys in usersById, so their title comes back as @"". The story composer's chat picker in src/TGStoriesViewController.m:2041-2043 does `NSString *title = TGStoryString(chat, @"title"); if (title.length == 0) continue;` — every channel row is silently dropped, so the user can never post a story as a channel, and if the own user record is not yet cached the action sheet appears with zero options. The same wrong helper is used at TGClient+Stories.m:441 (story viewer names: channel reposters show blank), :801 (hiddenStoryPosters) and :1183 (storyNotificationExceptions, which are chat ids).
fix: Add one shared name-for-message-sender helper and use it at all four sites: for id > 0 use -nameForUserId:, for id < 0 look the id up in self.chatsById[@(id)][@"title"] (TGClient+Private.h:25) and fall back to scanning client.chats/archivedChats — TGClient+Reactions.m:101 TGReactionSenderName() already implements exactly this and is the correct version.

what: streamFile:offset:count:completion: treats the file's `prefixSize` as bytes available at the requested offset: `long long available = [file[@"prefixSize"] longLongValue]; long long wanted = available < count ? available : count;`
failure: `prefixSize` is TDLib's local.downloaded_prefix_size, which is counted from local.download_offset, not from the caller's `offset`. When the file already has bytes from a previous range (download_offset = 0) and the player asks for offset = 2_000_000, prefixSize can be larger than what actually exists at that offset, so -readFile:offset:count: is issued with a count that runs past the downloaded region; readFilePart returns an error, the completion gets nil, and the AVAssetResourceLoader range fails — video playback stalls with no retry.
fix: Compute the availability relative to the request: `long long base = [file[@"downloadOffset"] longLongValue]; long long end = base + [file[@"prefixSize"] longLongValue]; long long available = end - offset;` (clamp to 0), or simply re-call -downloadedPrefixSizeForFile:offset: after the download completes and use that value as `wanted`.

what: TGFileOfMessageContent reads a photo size without a type guard: `file = TGFilesDict([sizes lastObject][@"photo"]);` — every other branch in this function wraps its lookups in TGFilesDict(), this one subscripts the raw last element.
failure: If TDLib's `photo.sizes` vector ever contains anything other than a dictionary (malformed/unexpected reply, or a future schema where sizes carries plain values), `-objectForKeyedSubscript:` is sent to e.g. an NSString or NSNumber and the app dies with 'unrecognized selector sent to instance' while building the downloads list in searchDownloadsWithQuery:.
fix: Change to `file = TGFilesDict(TGFilesDict([sizes lastObject])[@"photo"]);`, matching the guarded style used in the messageDocument/messageVideo branches above it and in TGClient+Stories.m:79.

what: The reaction watch timer polls one full getMessage per watched message every tick: inside -tgReactionWatchTick: `for (NSString *key in [TGReactionWatches allKeys]) { ... [self reactionChipsForMessage:messageId inChat:chatId completion:...] }` with TGReactionWatchInterval = 5.0.
failure: TGChatViewController creates a TGReactionChipsView per reacted bubble (src/TGChatViewController.m:5183-5192) and each one registers a watch (src/TGReactionPickerView.m:1870). A chat screen with 10 reacted messages visible issues 10 getMessage round trips every 5 seconds, forever, on a single-core A5 — each reply is a full message JSON parsed on the main queue. Scrolling a busy group chat becomes visibly janky and the radio never idles, draining the battery.
fix: Replace the poll with the TDLib push: handle `updateMessageInteractionInfo` in TGClient -handleUpdate: (it is currently not handled anywhere — `grep updateMessageInteractionInfo src` returns nothing), look the (chat_id, message_id) up in TGReactionWatches and fire the block from the update. Keep the timer only as a fallback with a much longer interval.

what: -setReactionWatchInterval: only writes the static `TGReactionWatchInterval = seconds < 2.0 ? 2.0 : seconds;`, but -tgStartReactionWatchTimer (line 539-547) reads that value once when it creates the NSTimer and returns early ever after (`if (TGReactionWatchTimer) return;`).
failure: Calling setReactionWatchInterval: after any chip view has started watching has no effect at all — the poll keeps running at whatever interval was in force when the first watch was registered. The method has no callers today, so it is both dead and broken; the first caller will silently get nothing.
fix: Either delete the method and its header declaration, or make it invalidate and rebuild the timer: `[TGReactionWatchTimer invalidate]; TGReactionWatchTimer = nil; if (TGReactionWatches.count) [self tgStartReactionWatchTimer];`.

what: -setStoryPreloading:onNetwork: builds the new settings from a preset instead of the current ones: `NSDictionary *base = TGStoryDict(presets[@"low"]); ... settings[@"preload_stories"] = @(preload); ... setAutoDownloadSettings`.
failure: Toggling story preloading overwrites the user's whole auto-download configuration for that network with the 'low' preset — max photo/video/other file sizes, video_upload_bitrate and use_less_data_for_calls all silently reset. Additionally TGStoryNetworkType() (line 253) maps everything that is not @"wifi" to networkTypeMobile, so the roaming and 'other' network types can never be addressed.

what: The same four-helper quartet is written independently in each file of this area: TGStoryIsError/TGStoryArray/TGStoryDict/TGStoryString (Stories.m:4-19), TGIsError/TGArray/TGDict/TGString (Stickers.m:4-19), TGFilesIsError/TGFilesArray/TGFilesDict/TGFilesString (Files.m:19-34), plus hand-rolled variants inline in Reactions.m (lines 262-263, 282-283, 334-335, 372-373, 641-642 all re-inline `![result isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class] || [result[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"error"]`).

All three isError variants also send -isEqualToString: to an unchecked `result[@"@type"]`, which crashes if TDLib ever returns a non-string there.

YES : [t isEqualToString:@"error"];`), delete the per-file copies, and replace the five inline error checks in Reactions.m with it.

what: TGFlattenSticker decides animation by negation: `@"isAnimated" : @(![format isEqualToString:@"stickerFormatWebp"])` where `format` defaults to @"" when the sticker object has no `format` member (line 47).
failure: Any sticker whose `format` field is missing or arrives under an unexpected type is reported as isAnimated = YES. Callers treat animated stickers as undecodable on this device, so a perfectly ordinary static WebP sticker is rendered as a blank/placeholder cell instead of the image.
fix: Invert the test to a positive one: `BOOL animated = [format isEqualToString:@"stickerFormatTgs"] || [format isEqualToString:@"stickerFormatWebm"];` so an unknown or missing format degrades to the static path.

what: TGMsgTopic() wraps the caller's `threadId` as a legacy message thread: `return @{@"@type" : @"messageTopicThread", @"message_thread_id" : @(threadId)};` — but the value every caller actually supplies is a forum_topic_id, not a message_thread_id. TGClient+MessageContent.m:243-244 wraps the very same argument as `@{@"@type" : @"messageTopicForum", @"forum_topic_id" : @(threadId)}`. The two files disagree about the shape of the same value and Messages.m is the wrong one.
failure: TGChatViewController.threadId is assigned at src/TGTopicsViewController.m:1027 from the topic row's @"threadId" key, which TGClient+Forums.m:71-72 fills with `info[@"forum_topic_id"]` (TGClient+Forums.h:6-9 states explicitly that forum_topic_id is an int32 that is NOT a message_thread_id). Forum topic ids are small ints (1, 2, 3...). So sending a message inside a forum topic builds `topic_id = {messageTopicThread, message_thread_id: 3}`. TDLib resolves message_thread_id 3 as a message id, finds no such thread, and answers error 400 "Message thread not found"; -sendText:toChat:thread:replyTo:options:completion: then calls its completion with nil and the message is never sent. The same wrong topic object is used by -forwardMessages:...(line 569), -setDraftText:replyTo:inChat:thread: (line 608), -clearDraftInChat:thread: (line 621) and -sendChatAction:toChat:thread: (line 851), so in a forum topic replies fail, forwards fail, drafts are never stored and the typing indicator never appears.
fix: Change TGMsgTopic to build the forum shape used by the rest of the codebase: `return @{@"@type" : @"messageTopicForum", @"forum_topic_id" : @((int32_t)threadId)};`. Keep it in one place — better still, delete TGMsgTopic and expose the existing TGClient+MessageContent helper, so there is a single definition of "what threadId means". (src/TGClient.m:955-966 -historyForChat:thread: has the same mistake, using threadId as a getMessageThreadHistory message_id; fix that in the same pass or the topic screen loads an empty history.)

what: Three independent message flatteners exist for the same TDLib `message` object, each with a different key set: TGMsgBrief (TGClient+Messages.m:52, keys id/text/kind/date/outgoing/senderId), TGSavedFlattenMessage (TGClient+SavedMessages.m:77, keys id/text/date/outgoing/senderId/senderChatId/isPinned/tags — no "kind") and TGFlattenMessage (TGClient.m:625, ~25 keys). The comment at TGClient+Messages.m:50-51 admits the split. The preview helpers are duplicated too: TGSavedPreview (SavedMessages.m:16) vs TGForumsMessagePreview (TGClient+Forums.m) vs the text extraction inside TGMsgBrief. Likewise three error predicates: TGMsgIsError (Messages.m:4), TGMCIsError (MessageContent.m:23) and the inline `![result[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"error"]` at SavedMessages.m:215/266/321/468.
failure: The dictionaries are not interchangeable. TGMsgBrief sets @"text" to "" for a caption-less photo; TGSavedFlattenMessage sets it to the literal "Photo"; TGFlattenMessage additionally supplies @"kind". Any row renderer fed from the wrong producer either draws the string "Photo" as if it were the user's typed text, or reads a @"kind" that is absent and falls into its text branch. Concretely, -propertiesOfMessage:inChat:completion: (Messages.m:412-415) derives canTranslate from TGMsgBrief's @"text", so a media message whose caption the chat screen displays via TGFlattenMessage still reports canTranslate correctly only by luck of both readers happening to look at content.caption.
fix: Promote one flattener. Move TGFlattenMessage out of TGClient.m's file scope into TGClient+Private.h as `TGFlattenMessage(NSDictionary *)`, delete TGMsgBrief and TGSavedFlattenMessage, and have TGMsgBriefList/savedMessagesTopicHistory call it; keep the Saved-Messages-only extras (senderChatId, isPinned, tags) as a thin wrapper that adds those three keys on top. Same for the error predicate: keep TGMsgIsError in TGClient+Private.h and delete TGMCIsError and the four inline copies.

failure: No runtime failure — this is pure weight. It also actively misleads: -sendPhotoAlbumAtPaths:toChat:caption:completion: (Messages.m) and -sendPhotoAlbumAtPaths:toChat:thread:caption:completion: (MessageContent.m:540) are two different album senders with incompatible completion types (NSArray* vs NSInteger), and a future caller typing the shorter one silently loses topic routing.

Keep -pinnedMessageIdInChat:completion: (it is the body of -isMessagePinned:) but make it file-static or move it below a `#pragma mark - private`. what: -markRead:inChat:source: maps the @"thread" source to the legacy thread constant: `if ([source isEqualToString:@"thread"]) type = @"messageSourceMessageThreadHistory";`. The bundled schema also has `messageSourceForumTopicHistory` (td_api.tl:3186), which is the correct source when the history being viewed is a forum topic — the only kind of thread this app opens (see finding 1).
failure: TDLib uses the message source to decide which unread counter to clear. Marking forum-topic messages read with messageSourceMessageThreadHistory clears the wrong counter, so the topic row in TGTopicsViewController keeps showing an unread badge after the user has read the topic.
fix: Add a branch: `else if ([source isEqualToString:@"topic"]) type = @"messageSourceForumTopicHistory";` and have TGChatViewController pass @"topic" when self.threadId != 0, or simply change the @"thread" mapping to messageSourceForumTopicHistory once finding 1 establishes that threadId is always a forum topic id.

what: TGSavedFlattenTopic resolves the title of a savedMessagesTopicTypeSavedFromChat topic with the user-name cache: `NSString *known = [[TGClient shared] nameForUserId:originChatId];` where originChatId came from `type[@"chat_id"]` (td_api.tl:3867 `savedMessagesTopicTypeSavedFromChat chat_id:int53`).
failure: chat_id for anything forwarded from a group or channel is a negative id (-100...) that is never a key in usersById, so nameForUserId returns nil and @"title" stays @"". TGSavedMessagesViewController then draws a Saved Messages topic row with an empty title for every message forwarded from a channel or group — only forwards from private users get a name.
fix: Fall back to the chat cache when the user lookup misses: after line 130, `if (!title.length) title = [[TGClient shared] titleForChatId:originChatId] ?: @"";` (or issue a getChat for the id and cache it), and only then leave it empty.

what: -loadSavedMessagesTopicsWithLimit:completion: guesses how long TDLib will take to deliver the topics: `dispatch_after(dispatch_time(DISPATCH_TIME_NOW, (int64_t)(0.35 * NSEC_PER_SEC)), dispatch_get_main_queue(), ^{ ... completion(me ? [me cachedSavedMessagesTopics] : ...); });`. loadSavedMessagesTopics returns Ok immediately (td_api.tl:11641) and the actual topics arrive later as updateSavedMessagesTopic updates.
failure: On a cold start on an A5 with a slow network the updates have not arrived after 350ms, so the completion hands back an empty array; TGSavedMessagesViewController.m:536 then calls -applyTopics:@[] and stops the spinner, showing an empty Saved Messages screen. It self-heals only because the screen also installs a topics-changed handler in viewWillAppear — if that handler has been nil'd by a second controller's dealloc (line 421 nils the single file-static slot unconditionally), the empty state is permanent until the user leaves and re-enters.
fix: Drop the dispatch_after. Call the completion synchronously with the current cache and rely on the topics-changed handler for the fill-in; and make -setSavedMessagesTopicsChangedHandler: keyed per observer (or have TGSavedMessagesViewController's dealloc only clear the slot when it still owns it) so one controller's dealloc cannot silence another's.

what: -privacyRuleDetailed:completion: latches its base-value flag on ANY unrecognised rule type: `else if (!haveBase){ haveBase = YES; if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleAllowAll"]) value = @"everybody"; else if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleAllowContacts"]) value = @"contacts"; }` — haveBase is set to YES before the type is known to be one of the three handled shapes, so the real base rule that follows is skipped and `value` keeps its @"nobody" default.
failure: td_api.tl:8841-8871 defines eleven rule types; four of them are not handled by any branch here (userPrivacySettingRuleAllowBots, userPrivacySettingRuleAllowPremiumUsers, userPrivacySettingRuleRestrictContacts, userPrivacySettingRuleRestrictBots). TDLib returns rules most-specific-first, so a Last Seen setting of 'Everybody except bots' comes back as [RestrictBots, AllowAll]. RestrictBots hits the else-if, sets haveBase=YES, and AllowAll is then ignored: privacyRuleDetailed reports value="nobody". TGPrivacyViewController.m:1094-1100 stores that into strongSelf.value and shows a checkmark on 'Nobody'. When the user then taps 'Contacts' (TGPrivacyViewController.m:1212) the app writes [RestrictUsers?, AllowContacts] and the RestrictBots rule the user had is destroyed — a privacy setting silently downgraded from a misread. The sibling implementation in TGClient+UserStatus.m:311-322 does this correctly (it only sets haveValue inside a matched branch), so the two files disagree about the same reply.
fix: Move `haveBase = YES;` inside each of the three matched branches, exactly as TGClient+UserStatus.m:311-322 does: `else if (!haveBase){ if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleAllowAll"]){ value = @"everybody"; haveBase = YES; } else if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleAllowContacts"]){ value = @"contacts"; haveBase = YES; } else if ([type isEqualToString:@"userPrivacySettingRuleRestrictAll"]){ value = @"nobody"; haveBase = YES; } }`.

what: -secretChatIdForChat: is a synchronous predicate backed by an asynchronously-filled cache and returns 0 on every cache miss: `NSNumber *known = TGSecretChatIds()[@(chatId)]; if (known) return [known intValue]; [self tgSecretFetchChat:chatId completion:nil]; return 0;`. The cache (TGSecretChatIds, line 4) is only ever written by -tgSecretRemember: from tgSecretFetchChat/createSecretChatWithUser/openSecretChatId, so a secret chat that exists on the server but has not been touched this launch always answers 'not a secret chat' the first time.
failure: Two live call sites are wrong on first use. (1) TGChatListViewController.m:1973 `if (!chatId || [[TGClient shared] secretChatIdForChat:chatId] == 0) return nil;` — after a cold launch every secret chat row renders with no handshake line ('waiting for X to come online' / 'exchanging encryption keys'), and because the method bails before the row is added to self.secretStatusesRequested nothing schedules a redraw; the line only appears if some unrelated event reloads the table later. (2) TGProfileViewController.m:693 `if (!self.chatId || ![[TGClient shared] isSecretChat:self.chatId]) [items addObject:@{@"title":@"Start secret chat"...}]` — opening the profile of an existing secret chat for the first time offers 'Start secret chat', and tapping it (TGProfileViewController.m:1489) calls createNewSecretChat and creates a duplicate second secret chat with the same user.
fix: Make the predicate honest and asynchronous, or prime the cache. Minimum fix: seed TGSecretChatIds from chat objects the client already has — call -tgSecretRemember: from TGClient's updateNewChat/updateChatLastMessage handling in TGClient.m -handleUpdate:, so every chat that appears in the chat list is classified before any row is drawn. Additionally, in TGChatListViewController.m:1973, when secretChatIdForChat: misses, do not `return nil` silently — the -tgSecretFetchChat: it kicks off should call back and trigger `[me.tableView reloadData]`; give tgSecretFetchChat a completion that posts a notification the chat list observes.

what: Three parallel privacy-rule APIs exist and two of them are wired to different screens: TGClient.m:2028 -privacyRule:completion: / TGClient.m:2046 -setPrivacyRule:to: (base rule only, fire-and-forget), TGClient+UserStatus.m:274/334 -privacyRuleDetail:completion: / -setPrivacyRule:to:allowUsers:restrictUsers:completion: (unused), and TGClient+Privacy.m:111/162 -privacyRuleDetailed:completion: / -setPrivacyRule:to:allowedUsers:restrictedUsers:completion:.
failure: TGSettingsViewController.m:2373 calls `[[TGClient shared] setPrivacyRule:setting to:value]` — TGClient.m:2046 builds `@"rules" : @[@{@"@type" : rule}]`, a one-element list with only the base rule. setUserPrivacySettingRules replaces the entire rule list, so any AllowUsers/RestrictUsers exception list the user built on the Privacy screen (TGPrivacyViewController.m:1212, which does pass them) is deleted server-side. Concretely: add five people to 'Never share my Last Seen', go back to Settings and flip Last Seen from Everybody to My Contacts, and all five exceptions are gone with no warning. TGClient.m:2036 `[rules[@"rules"] firstObject][@"@type"]` compounds it by reporting 'nobody' whenever the first rule is a RestrictUsers exception.
fix: Delete -privacyRule:completion: and -setPrivacyRule:to: from TGClient.m:2028-2058 (and their declarations at TGClient.h:212-214) and delete -privacyRuleDetail:completion: / -setPrivacyRule:to:allowUsers:restrictUsers:completion: from TGClient+UserStatus.m:274-363 (declarations at TGClient+UserStatus.h:69,77). Point TGSettingsViewController.m:508 at -privacyRuleDetailed:completion: (reading info[@"value"]) and TGSettingsViewController.m:2373 at -setPrivacyRule:to:allowedUsers:restrictedUsers:completion:, passing the allowedUserIds/restrictedUserIds it just read back unchanged so the exception lists survive.

what: Three session flatteners with divergent key names: TGPrivacySessionDict (TGClient+Privacy.m:38) emits @"ip", @"lastActive" and a pre-joined @"platform" (`platform + " " + system_version`); TGAccountFlattenSession (TGClient+Account.m:935) emits @"ipAddress", @"lastActiveDate", and separate @"platform" / @"systemVersion"; TGAccountSessionDict (TGClient+Account.m:128) is a third, shorter variant using @"ip" and a %@ %@ platform string.
failure: TGSessionsViewController populates its list from -activeSessionsWithCompletion: (Privacy shape) but refreshes the detail screen from -sessionInfoForId:completion: (Account shape, TGSessionsViewController.m:764). what: -checkUsernameAvailable:completion: checks an account username using the public-chat endpoint with chat_id 0: `[self request:@{ @"@type" : @"checkChatUsername", @"chat_id" : @(0), @"username" : username }`.
failure: td_api.tl:11553 documents chat_id as 'identifier of a supergroup or channel chat, or a private chat with self, or 0 if the chat is being created'. Passing 0 asks TDLib whether the name is free for a NEW PUBLIC GROUP, so the answer is filtered through the public-chat quota: a user who already owns the maximum number of public groups gets checkChatUsernameResultPublicChatsTooMany and the method reports @"too_many" for a username that is in fact perfectly available for their account, and on some accounts checkChatUsernameResultPublicGroupsUnavailable → @"unavailable". The username picker would refuse a valid name.
fix: Pass the private chat with self. Fetch the own user id once (getMe → id) and use it as chat_id, or resolve the Saved Messages chat id and pass that: `@"chat_id" : @(myUserId)`. Note this method currently has no callers, so fix it at the same time as wiring up the username editor, or delete it along with the other dead Contacts methods.

what: TGIsError sends isEqualToString: to an unchecked object: `return ![result isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class] || [result[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"error"];`. The same unguarded pattern is at TGClient+SecretChats.m:11 (TGScIsError) and at the raw comparisons in TGClient+Contacts.m:43 (`![u[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"user"]`), :138, :274, :384 and :650.
failure: If a reply ever carries a non-string under @"@type" — a corrupted frame, a future td_api change, or any object the client synthesises and passes through these helpers — the message lands on an NSNumber or NSArray and the app dies with 'unrecognized selector sent to instance'. The two sibling files in this same area already guard: TGClient+Account.m:7-10 checks `[type isKindOfClass:[NSString class]]` first and TGClient+UserStatus.m:24 routes through TGUSString. Contacts and SecretChats were written without it, so identical code has two different crash profiles.
fix: In TGClient+Contacts.m:22-25 and TGClient+SecretChats.m:11-14, route the type through the file's existing string coercion, matching TGClient+UserStatus.m:22-25: `return ![result isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class] || [TGString(result[@"@type"]) isEqualToString:@"error"];` (TGScString in SecretChats). Do the same at Contacts.m:43, :138, :274, :384 and :650, e.g. `![TGString(u[@"@type"]) isEqualToString:@"user"]`.

what: -countOnlineAmong:index:running:completion: walks the member list one TDLib round trip at a time — `[self request:@{@"@type" : @"getUser", @"user_id" : @(userId)} completion:^{ ... [weakSelf countOnlineAmong:userIds index:index + 1 ...]; }]` — and -groupOnlineSummaryForChat: (line 201) feeds it up to 50 supergroup members (line 255 `@"limit" : @(50)`).
failure: Fifty serialised getUser calls to produce one '128 members, 7 online' header line. Each reply is dispatch_async'd onto the main queue (TGClient.m:102), so on a single-core A5 the chat header takes tens of round trips to settle, and nothing caches the result or cancels the chain when the user leaves the chat — reopening the same group restarts all fifty. There is also no error check on the getBasicGroupFullInfo reply (line 232), so a failed lookup silently yields '0 members'.
fix: Replace the per-user walk with the counts TDLib already returns: for supergroups, supergroupFullInfo carries member_count (already read at line 250) — there is no separate online count in td_api, so either drop the ', N online' suffix or bound the probe to the members already resident in the client. If the online count is kept, cache the result per chatId with a short TTL, cap the probe at ~10 members, and guard the getBasicGroupFullInfo reply with TGUSIsError(full) before calling answer().

what: Most of TGClient+Contacts.m and the secret-chat capability layer are unreferenced. Contacts, zero external callers: -searchContacts:limit:completion: (219), -addContactWithUserId:... failure: Roughly 900 lines of compiled-in code no screen can reach, on a device with 40-60MB of usable RAM. Worse than the size cost: the secret-chat security surface is inert. -secretChat:allowsInputMessage: (the gate that blocks polls, checklists, forwards, stories, invoices and games in a secret chat) and -chatAllowsMessageEditing: are never consulted by the composer, and -selfDestructOptionForChat:seconds: is never attached to an outgoing message, so the self-destruct timer UI has no send path behind it. -encryptionKeyGridForChat: means there is no key-visualisation screen at all.
fix: Two separate decisions. (a) Delete the contact/profile helpers that no screen plans to use, together with their declarations in TGClient+Contacts.h and TGClient+SecretChats.h. (b) Do NOT delete the secret-chat gates — wire them up: call -secretChat:allowsInputMessage: in TGChatViewController before building any non-text inputMessage content, call -chatAllowsMessageEditing: before showing the Edit action in the message menu, and merge the dictionary from -selfDestructOptionForChat:seconds: into the sendMessage payload for secret chats.

what: Three parallel auto-download setters exist (TGClient+Network.m:513 -setAutoDownloadSettings:networkKind:completion:, TGClient+Storage.m:571 -setAutoDownloadSettings:forNetworkType:, TGClient+Files.m:580 -setAutoDownloadSettings:forNetwork:completion:) and they disagree on the input key vocabulary; the Files copy reads `from[@"lessDataForCalls"] ?: @NO` while Network's preset dictionaries emit `useLessDataForCalls` (TGClient+Network.m:153).
failure: TGClient+Files.h:213-218 documents the key as "lessDataForCalls" but tells the caller to obtain the dictionary from TGClient+Network's -autoDownloadPresetsWithCompletion:, which emits "useLessDataForCalls". Feeding a Network preset into the Files setter silently sends use_less_data_for_calls=false, and also defaults is_auto_download_enabled to @YES (line 586) where Network/Storage default to NO, so an empty dictionary turns auto-download ON instead of OFF.
fix: Delete -setAutoDownloadSettings:forNetwork:completion: from TGClient+Files.m/.h (it has no callers) and route everything through TGClient+Network.m's TGNetSettingsObject/TGNetSettingsDict pair; if it must stay, change line 594 to read from[@"useLessDataForCalls"] and line 586 default to @NO.

what: -setAutoDownloadSettings:forNetworkType: uses a third key vocabulary ("maxPhoto"/"maxVideo"/"maxOther") while Network uses "maxPhotoSize"/"maxVideoSize"/"maxOtherSize" (TGClient+Network.m:146-148), and it hard-codes `@"preload_stories" : @NO` (line 585) because TGStorageAutoDownloadFromPreset (line 105) never carries that field through.
failure: TGSettingsViewController.m:830 reads the Storage mirror while line 837 reads `preset[@"maxPhotoSize"]` from Network presets — the two halves of one settings row speak different dialects, so any future code that hands a Network preset to the Storage setter gets max_photo_file_size = 1 MB default instead of the preset value, and every write through Storage clears the server's preload_stories flag.
fix: Pick one vocabulary (Network's maxPhotoSize/maxVideoSize/maxOtherSize/preloadStories/useLessDataForCalls), rewrite TGStorageNormalizedAutoDownload (line 80), TGStorageAutoDownloadFromPreset (line 105) and the payload at lines 578-586 to use it, add a preloadStories passthrough, and update the doc block in TGClient+Storage.h:176.

what: -setAutosaveScope:photos:videos:maxVideoSize: (line 370) and -setAutosaveForChat:photos:videos:maxVideoSize: (line 382) are byte-for-byte duplicates of TGClient+Storage.m:621 -setAutosavePhotos:videos:maxVideoBytes:forScope: and TGClient+Storage.m:780 -setAutosavePhotos:videos:maxVideoBytes:forChat:, down to the same setAutosaveSettings payload.

The Storage pair clamps a non-positive size to 512 KB (Storage.m:637) while the AppSettings pair passes maxVideoSize straight through, so calling the AppSettings variant with 0 sends max_video_file_size=0 and silently disables video autosave, whereas the Storage variant with the same argument enables it at 512 KB. Only the Storage pair has callers; the AppSettings pair is dead.
fix: Delete -setAutosaveScope:photos:videos:maxVideoSize: and -setAutosaveForChat:photos:videos:maxVideoSize: plus TGASAutosaveScopeObject (AppSettings.m:139) from TGClient+AppSettings.m/.h; keep the Storage pair as the single autosave writer.

what: The whole TGClient (Calls) category is unreachable: of the 14 methods in TGClient+Calls.h only -rateCallId:rating:comment:problems:completion: has a caller anywhere in src/. -callLogWithOffset:, -frequentlyCalledContactsWithCompletion:, -groupCallServiceTextForContent:, -isGroupCallLink:, -clearCallLogRevoke:, -declineGroupCallInvitationInChat:, -callNetworkUsageWithCompletion:, -resetNetworkUsageWithCompletion:, -setSessionId:canAcceptCalls:, -sendDebugInformationForCallId:, -sendLogForCallId:, -rateCallInChat:, -removeFrequentlyCalledChat: have none.
failure: 390 lines of code, its string tables and its Objective-C metadata are linked into the binary and paged in at launch on a 512 MB device that has 40-60 MB of headroom, and no screen can ever reach any of it. The same is true of TGClient+Translation.m (10 of 13 public methods uncalled — the entire language-pack and speech-recognition surface, lines 214-413) and of the wallpaper/theme half of TGClient+AppSettings.m (12 of 17 public methods uncalled, lines 232-433).
fix: Either delete the uncalled methods from TGClient+Calls.m/.h, TGClient+Translation.m/.h (languagePacks*, languagePackInfo:, applyLanguagePack:, synchronizeLanguagePack:, languagePackStrings:, deleteLanguagePack:, recognizeSpeechForMessage:, speechTranscriptForMessage:, rateSpeechRecognitionForMessage:, translateMessages:) and TGClient+AppSettings.m/.h (setDefaultBackground*, searchBackgroundNamed:, shareUrlForBackgroundNamed:, removeInstalledBackgroundId:, resetInstalledBackgrounds, setChatThemeEmoji:, chatThemeEmojiForChat:, applicationConfigValueForKey:), or wire the screens that were supposed to use them. Do not leave them half-alive.

what: -storageUsageForChat: answers a per-chat question by fetching the global top-N list: `[self storageUsageByChatWithLimit:256 completion:...]` and then linear-scanning it for a matching chatId.
failure: getStorageStatistics with chat_limit:256 groups every chat outside the 256 largest into a single entry with chat_id == 0 (td_api.tl:9685). For a user with more than 256 cached chats, asking for the cache size of a small chat returns (0, 0) — the screen shows "0 bytes" and the Clear button looks like a no-op even though files exist. It also walks the entire file cache on an A5 for one number.
fix: Do not reuse the aggregate call. Either accept the imprecision explicitly by documenting the 256-chat ceiling in TGClient+Storage.h, or issue getStorageStatistics with a large chat_limit only once and cache the by_chat map, keyed by chat_id, instead of re-walking the cache per chat.

what: -writeScope:settings: rebuilds the full scopeNotificationSettings object on every write and hard-codes the story fields: `@"use_default_mute_stories" : @YES, @"mute_stories" : @NO, @"story_sound_id" : @(0), @"show_story_poster" : @NO`, while -notificationSettingsForScope: (line 66) never reads them back. `use_default_mute_stories` is not even a field of scopeNotificationSettings (td_api.tl:3348 — it belongs to chatNotificationSettings).
failure: Toggling any unrelated switch on the Notifications page (TGSettingsViewController.m:1873 -> -updateScope:values:completion:) resets the account's story notification settings on the server: mute_stories and show_story_poster go to false and story_sound_id to 0, clobbering whatever the user set from a modern client.
fix: Add mute_stories / story_sound_id / show_story_poster to TGNotifScopeSettingsFrom (line 53) as "muteStories"/"storySoundId"/"showStoryPoster", read them back in -writeScope: from the merged dictionary instead of constants, and drop the bogus use_default_mute_stories key.

what: Four of the seven error predicates in this layer send isEqualToString: to an unchecked value: `[((NSDictionary *)result)[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"error"]` (Calls.m:6, AppSettings.m:6, Storage.m:55, Notifications.m:17). TGClient+Network.m:29-32 and TGClient+Translation.m:7-9 do type-check first, so the codebase already knows better.
failure: Any reply whose "@type" is not a string — a malformed frame, or a future TDLib object where the code walks a nested dictionary through the same predicate, e.g. Calls.m:270 `[entry[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"networkStatisticsEntryCall"]` on an entry whose @type came back as a number — raises -[__NSCFNumber isEqualToString:]: unrecognized selector and kills the app instead of being treated as an error result.
fix: Replace the bodies of TGCallsIsError, TGASIsError, TGStorageFailed and TGNotifIsError with the guarded form used in TGClient+Network.m:26-33: fetch @type, `if (![type isKindOfClass:[NSString class]]) return YES;`, then compare. Same guard for the bare nested comparisons at Calls.m:136, Calls.m:270 and Storage.m:520.

what: Network-type name mapping is written twice with different accepted inputs: TGStorageNetworkTypeName (Storage.m:20) accepts "cellular" and "roaming", TGNetNetworkTypeName (Network.m:65) accepts "mobileroaming" but not "cellular"/"roaming" alone. Likewise TGNetString/TGNetNumber/TGNetArray/TGNetDict, TGCallsString/TGCallsNumber/TGCallsArray/TGCallsDict, TGStorageDictionary/TGStorageArray, TGTrString/TGTrNumber/TGTrArray/TGTrDict and TGASDict are five identical copies of the same four coercion helpers.
failure: TGClient+Storage.h:200 documents the network names as "wifi"/"mobile"/"roaming"/"other" and Storage.m:700 defaults to exactly that list; passing "roaming" to the Network category's -setAutoDownloadSettings:networkKind: (Network.m:513) instead maps to networkTypeOther, so a roaming preset is written to the wrong TDLib network bucket and never takes effect while roaming.
fix: Keep one mapping function (the Storage one, which accepts the documented vocabulary plus aliases), expose it from TGClient+Private.h, and delete TGNetNetworkTypeName; do the same for the four coercion helpers so all seven files share one set.

what: The chatindex URL handler hardcodes tab 0 as the chat list -- `tabs.selectedIndex = 0; UINavigationController *nc = tabs.viewControllers[0]; [nc popToRootViewControllerAnimated:NO];` -- but RootViewController installs the tabs as `@[contactsNC, chatsNC, settingsNC]` (src/RootViewController.m:58) with chats at index 1.
failure: itglegacy://chatindex/3 switches to the Contacts tab and pushes TGChatViewController (or TGTopicsViewController) onto the Contacts navigation stack. The chat opens over the contacts list, the back button returns to Contacts, and every subsequent tap/, holdrow/ or profile/ URL that resolves `tabs.viewControllers[tabs.selectedIndex]` now operates on the Contacts stack. All scripted chat testing runs against the wrong tab.
fix: Replace the two literal 0s at src/AppDelegate.m:300-301 with the chat-list tab index 1 (matching RootViewController's order), i.e. `tabs.selectedIndex = 1; UINavigationController *nc = tabs.viewControllers[1];`. Better: define a shared constant (e.g. `TGTabIndexChats = 1`) in RootViewController.h and use it in both files so the two cannot drift again.

what: The auth-state switch only creates the login UI for TGAuthStateWaitPhoneNumber / Closed / LoggingOut. `case TGAuthStateWaitCode: [me.loginVC showCodeStepWithPhoneNumber:me.currentPhoneNumber];` and `case TGAuthStateWaitPassword: [me.loginVC showPasswordStep];` assume self.loginVC already exists, and TGAuthStateWaitRegistration falls into `default: break;`.
failure: TDLib persists auth state in its database. Relaunching the app after the login code was requested (or after the code was accepted and 2FA is pending) makes handleAuthState (src/TGClient.m:438) emit authorizationStateWaitCode / WaitPassword as the very first state. At that moment self.loginVC is nil, because didFinishLaunchingWithOptions only called showLoadingUI. The two messages go to nil, no screen is ever installed, and the app sits on the grey spinner from showLoadingUI forever with no way to finish logging in short of deleting the TDLib database.
fix: In src/AppDelegate.m:110-115, call `[me showLoginUI];` before addressing me.loginVC in the WaitCode, WaitPassword and WaitRegistration cases (showLoginUI is already idempotent -- it returns early when loginVC exists). Add an explicit `case TGAuthStateWaitRegistration:` that also calls showLoginUI instead of letting it hit `default`.

what: A second, different `tab` handler exists: `if ([host isEqualToString:@"tab"]){ ... tabs.selectedIndex = MIN((NSUInteger)[arg integerValue], tabs.viewControllers.count - 1); }`. The first `tab` handler at line 268 already returns YES, so this block is unreachable.
failure: Unreachable code that silently disagrees with the live handler: the dead one clamps out-of-range indices and does not pop to root, the live one rejects out-of-range indices and does pop. Anyone reading or editing the second copy changes nothing at runtime, and a future edit to it will appear to have no effect. `MIN((NSUInteger)[arg integerValue], ...)` in the dead copy would also turn itglegacy://tab/-1 into index 2 via unsigned wrap.
fix: Delete src/AppDelegate.m:574-583 (the comment plus the whole second `if ([host isEqualToString:@"tab"])` block). Keep the handler at line 268.

what: `@protocol TGScrollToTopTarget` / `- (void)scrollToTopRequested;` is declared here and dispatched at line 97-98 (`if ([controller respondsToSelector:@selector(scrollToTopRequested)]) [(id<TGScrollToTopTarget>)controller scrollToTopRequested];`), but no class in src/ implements scrollToTopRequested -- grep over src/*.m finds only these two lines.
failure: Tapping the already-selected tab (the standard iOS scroll-to-top gesture, wired through TGTabBar -> tabBarSelectedItem:) always fails the respondsToSelector: check and does nothing. The feature the code is written for silently does not exist on any screen.
fix: Either implement `- (void)scrollToTopRequested` on TGChatListViewController, TGContactsViewController and TGSettingsViewController (`[self.tableView setContentOffset:CGPointMake(0, -self.tableView.contentInset.top) animated:YES]`), or delete the protocol at src/RootViewController.m:14-16 and the else branch at lines 93-99.

what: `[TGHacks setLayoutDelegateForContainerView:self.view.subviews[0] layoutDelegate:self.layoutDelegate];` (also re-run from reassociateLayoutDelegate on every viewDidLayoutSubviews). The association is only ever read by the swizzled -layoutSubviewsTG, and TGHacks swizzles exactly one class: `@[@[@"UILayoutContainerView", [TGLayoutContainerView class]]]` (src/TGHacks.m:61-62). self.view.subviews[0] of a UITabBarController is a UITransitionView, which is not swizzled.
failure: The associated object on the transition view is set and retained on every layout pass but never read by anything, so it has no effect. The original 2013 source (TelegraphKit/TGHacks.m:329-332) also registered TGTransitionView, TGNavigationTransitionView and TGViewControllerWrapperView; that part was dropped in the port, leaving the caller half-wired.
fix: Either drop the second association (src/RootViewController.m:29-30 and the reassociateLayoutDelegate/viewDidLayoutSubviews pair at 33-41), or restore the missing swizzle pairs in src/TGHacks.m:61-63 by adding `TGFullscreenContainerClass(TGTransitionView)` and an `@[@"UITransitionView", [TGTransitionView class]]` entry to classPairs.

what: The touch/ handler reimplements TGTabBar's hit test with a hardcoded tab count: `int index = MAX(0, MIN((int)3 - 1, (int)(point.x / (view.frame.size.width / 3))));`. TGTabBar already has `- (int)indexForLocation:(CGPoint)location` (src/TGTabBar.m:90-95) which does the same arithmetic from self.buttonViews.count.
failure: Two copies of the same formula, one of them with the tab count frozen at 3. Changing the number of tabs makes itglegacy://touch on the tab bar select the wrong tab while real finger taps still work, which reads as a UI bug rather than a harness bug. The copy also uses `point` in window coordinates without converting into the tab bar's space; that happens to be correct only because the bar sits at x=0 spanning the full width.
fix: Declare `- (int)indexForLocation:(CGPoint)location;` in src/TGTabBar.h and in src/AppDelegate.m:362 call `[(TGTabBar *)view indexForLocation:[view convertPoint:point fromView:nil]]` instead of the inline expression.

what: The URL-scheme doc comment states `itglegacy://tab/N switch to tab N (0 chats, 1 contacts, 2 settings)`, but RootViewController orders the tabs contacts(0), chats(1), settings(2) (src/RootViewController.m:58) and defaults to index 1.
failure: Anyone scripting the device from this comment sends itglegacy://tab/0 expecting the chat list and lands on Contacts; this is almost certainly the origin of the chatindex bug above. Documentation and code disagree about the same data.
fix: Correct the comment at src/AppDelegate.m:232 (and the duplicate line 231 entry) to read `0 contacts, 1 chats, 2 settings`.

what: teardown clears the process-wide incoming-call handler that AppDelegate installed once at launch: `if ([TGCall shared].onStateChanged != nil) [TGCall shared].onStateChanged = nil;` (teardown is called from viewWillDisappear:194 and dealloc:222).
failure: AppDelegate.m:26 TGWatchForIncomingCalls() sets [TGCall shared].onStateChanged and is called exactly once, from application:didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: (AppDelegate.m:57). TGCallViewController.m:160 overwrites that same single-slot property with its own block, and teardown nils it. After the first call of any kind (incoming or outgoing) ends, [TGCall shared].onStateChanged is nil forever: a subsequent TGCallStatePending update fires no handler, so no incoming call screen is ever presented again for the rest of the process lifetime.
fix: Make TGCallViewController save the previous handler before overwriting (`self.savedStateHandler = [TGCall shared].onStateChanged;` at line 160) and restore it in teardown instead of assigning nil, exactly as TGMediaViewController does for onFileProgress (TGMediaViewController.m:2199-2216). Better: expose TGWatchForIncomingCalls as a class method on AppDelegate and re-arm it from teardown.

what: AVCaptureFileOutput's completion delegate does main-thread-only work on AVFoundation's private delegate queue: `- (void)captureOutput:...didFinishRecordingToOutputFileAtURL:...` calls `[self stopTimer]` (line 524 -> `[self.timer invalidate]` line 413) and `[self failWithCode:code]` (line 551 -> `[delegate videoRecorder:self didFailWithError:error]` line 104).
failure: didFinishRecordingToOutputFileAtURL: is delivered on AVFoundation's internal serial queue, not the main queue. (a) NSTimer -invalidate must be sent from the thread that scheduled the timer (startTimer:405 schedules on the main run loop); invalidating from another thread leaves the timer firing against a torn-down recorder or over-releases it. (b) failWithCode: reaches TGVideoCaptureViewController.m:421 videoRecorder:didFailWithError:, which calls -resetToCamera and mutates UIKit views off the main thread - on iOS 6.1/armv7 this produces missing redraws, autolayout/CALayer corruption, and intermittent crashes when the user stops a too-short or failed recording. Note the success path (deliverFileAtPath:581) does hop to the main queue, so the failure path is inconsistent with the rest of the class.
fix: Wrap the entire body of captureOutput:didFinishRecordingToOutputFileAtURL:fromConnections:error: (lines 523-555) in `dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), ^{ ... })` with a `__weak typeof(self) weakSelf` guard, matching deliverFileAtPath:. Then stopTimer, discardOutputFile, failWithCode: and deliverFileAtPath: all run on main.

what: Instant View block heights are measured on a background queue: `dispatch_async(dispatch_get_global_queue(...), ^{ ... [TGInstantViewController heightForBlock:block] ... })` (line 371-374), and heightForBlock: uses UIStringDrawing - `[caption sizeWithFont:[UIFont systemFontOfSize:13] constrainedToSize:... lineBreakMode:...]` (line 476) plus `+fontForKind:` (line 387).
failure: NSString UIStringDrawing (-sizeWithFont:constrainedToSize:lineBreakMode:) is not thread-safe before iOS 7; the target here is iOS 6.1.3. Opening an Instant View article with captions/paragraphs measures dozens of strings concurrently with main-thread text drawing, which intermittently deadlocks or crashes inside the shared WebCore/CoreText font cache, and otherwise returns garbage heights that make rows overlap.
fix: Do the measuring pass on the main queue: replace the global-queue dispatch at line 371 with a straight loop on main (heights are cheap - the article is at most a few hundred blocks), or precompute text sizes with CoreText (CTFramesetterSuggestFrameSizeWithConstraints), which is thread-safe on iOS 6, instead of -sizeWithFont:.

what: A block-based notification observer is registered without keeping the token: `[[NSNotificationCenter defaultCenter] addObserverForName:TGThemeChangedNotification object:nil queue:[NSOperationQueue mainQueue] usingBlock:^(NSNotification *note){ ... }];` and dealloc (line 1688-1691) only does `[[NSNotificationCenter defaultCenter] removeObserver:self]`.
failure: addObserverForName:... returns an opaque observer object which is what must be passed to removeObserver:; removeObserver:self does not unregister it. Every chat opened registers one more permanent observer that the notification center retains forever. On a theme change all of them fire: [TGIcons flush] runs once per chat ever opened, plus a reloadData against each dead controller's table via the weak reference. On a 512MB/40-60MB-usable iPhone 4S this is an unbounded observer + block leak and a visible stall on theme switch. TGChatListViewController.m:976 does this correctly (stores self.themeObserver and removes it in dealloc:1173) - this file simply dropped that.
fix: Add `@property (nonatomic, strong) id themeObserver;` to the class extension, assign the return value at line 1432 (`self.themeObserver = [[NSNotificationCenter defaultCenter] addObserverForName:...]`), and in dealloc add `if (self.themeObserver) [[NSNotificationCenter defaultCenter] removeObserver:self.themeObserver];` before the existing removeObserver:self.

what: TGMediaViewController save/restores the single global progress hook (`void (^previous)(NSInteger, float) = client.onFileProgress; self.savedProgressBlock = previous;` line 2199-2200, restored in removeProgressHook line 2214), but TGChatViewController.m:2338 overwrites the same property unconditionally (`[TGClient shared].onFileProgress = ^(NSInteger updatedId, float progress){ ... };`) and never restores or clears it.
failure: Sequence: open a chat, tap a media file (beginDownloadHUD installs the chat's block at TGChatViewController.m:2338), open the media viewer (addProgressHook saves the chat block and chains), start another download from the chat (TGChatViewController.m:2338 replaces the chained block outright), close the media viewer -> removeProgressHook writes the stale saved block back over the chat's current one. The chat's download HUD freezes at whatever percentage it had reached and never updates, even though the download continues. The reverse order silently drops the media viewer's chaining.
fix: Give TGClient a small array of progress observers (add/remove by token) instead of the single `onFileProgress` block, and convert both TGChatViewController.m:2338 and TGMediaViewController.m:2204 to register/unregister. Minimum fix: make TGChatViewController chain the same way the media viewer does (save the previous block in beginDownloadHUD, call it from inside the new block, restore it in endDownloadHUD at line 2347).

what: `-request:completion:` stores the completion in self.pendingRequests (line 152) and only then calls -send:, which can silently drop the request: `NSData *data = [NSJSONSerialization dataWithJSONObject:request options:0 error:&err]; if (!data){ NSLog(@"TGClient: cannot encode %@: %@", request, err); return; }` (TGClient.m:116-121). There is also no timeout and no flush of pendingRequests on TDLib shutdown / logout.
failure: Any request dictionary carrying a non-JSON value - an NSNull or NSDate that leaked out of a TDLib reply and was fed straight back in, an NSString built from invalid UTF-8, or a nil-boxed id - fails to encode. Nothing is ever sent, so no reply with that @extra ever arrives, so the completion sits in pendingRequests forever. Every caller that shows a spinner or HUD and hides it only in the completion (e.g. TGLoginViewController -setBusy:, TGMediaViewController download chrome) spins forever with no error path. The same happens for every in-flight request if TDLib is stopped, and the retained completions keep their captured controllers alive.
fix: Make -send: report failure (`- (BOOL)send:`) and in -request:completion: remove the pending entry and invoke the completion with a synthetic error object (`@{@"@type": @"error", @"code": @(-1), @"message": @"encode failed"}`) when the send fails. Additionally, on shutdown/logout drain self.pendingRequests, calling each completion with the same synthetic error, and consider a per-request watchdog that fires the completion with an error after N seconds.

what: The chat-action handler stored on the TGClient singleton captures a view strongly: `[TGClient shared].onChatAction = ^(int64_t chatId, NSString *action){ if (chatId != weakSelf.chatId) return; subtitle.text = action ?: restingSubtitle; };` - `subtitle` is the local UILabel created in -buildTitleView, and the block is never cleared (dealloc at line 1688 only invalidates the playback timer and removes NSNotificationCenter observers).
failure: The singleton keeps the block, and the block keeps the subtitle UILabel of the last chat's title view alive for the rest of the process. Worse, the block keeps writing into a label belonging to a popped controller whenever a chat action update arrives for a chat whose id happens to match (weakSelf is nil after dealloc, so chatId != 0 usually short-circuits, but a chatId of 0 in a malformed update writes into the dead view).
fix: Capture the label weakly (`__weak UILabel *weakSubtitle = subtitle;`) and resolve both weakSelf and weakSubtitle inside the block, bailing if either is nil; and clear `[TGClient shared].onChatAction = nil` in -dealloc (or better, set it in viewWillAppear alongside installMessageHandler and clear it in viewWillDisappear).

what: The chat-list layout preference is implemented twice, with two different NSUserDefaults keys and two different value types. Settings owns `static NSString *const TGSettingsChatListLayoutKey = @"TGChatListLayout";` (line 72) and stores an NSString "a"/"b" via +setChatListLayout: (line 763-772). The chat list owns `static NSString *const TGChatListFolderStyleKey = @"TGChatListFolderStyle";` (TGChatListViewController.m:481) and reads an NSInteger 0/1 via TGChatListFolderStyle() (TGChatListViewController.m:497-500).
failure: User opens Settings -> Chat List Layout and taps "Chooser in the Title". +setChatListLayout: writes @"a" under key "TGChatListLayout" and posts TGSettingsChatListLayoutChangedNotification. Nothing reads that key and nothing observes that notification (grep for both names returns only TGSettingsViewController.m). TGChatListFolderStyle() still reads "TGChatListFolderStyle", finds nothing, and returns the TGChatListFolderStyleStrip default. The chat list never changes, and the checkmark in Settings does move, so the setting looks applied and is completely inert.
fix: Delete the parallel implementation in TGSettingsViewController.m: remove TGSettingsChatListLayoutKey (line 72), TGSettingsChatListLayoutChangedNotification (lines 81-82), +chatListLayout/+chatListLayoutTitle/+setChatListLayout: (lines 746-772). Make +chatListLayout read and +setChatListLayout: write the integer key @"TGChatListFolderStyle" using the values TGChatListFolderStyleChooser=0 / TGChatListFolderStyleStrip=1 defined at TGChatListViewController.m:483-484, keeping the existing title array order (index 0 = Chooser, index 1 = Strip). Move those two constants plus TGChatListFolderStyle() into a shared header so both files use one definition, and have TGChatListViewController observe the change notification and call -reloadData.

what: The "show stories" preference is implemented twice under two different keys. Settings: `static NSString *const TGSettingsStoriesEnabledKey = @"TGStoriesEnabled";` written by +setStoriesEnabled: (line 725) and read by +storiesEnabled (line 717). Chat list: `static NSString *const TGChatListStoriesTrayKey = @"TGShowStoriesTray";` (TGChatListViewController.m:481-480) read by TGStoriesTrayEnabled() (TGChatListViewController.m:493-495), which is the only gate on the tray (used at lines 937, 1191, 1590).
failure: Turning the Stories switch off writes NO to "TGStoriesEnabled". TGStoriesTrayEnabled() reads "TGShowStoriesTray", which no code in src/ ever writes, so `stored` is nil and it returns the YES default forever. The stories tray stays on screen (and keeps downloading story avatars, ~82pt of the chat list and a per-poster file download on a 512MB device) no matter what the user chooses. Symmetrically, TGSettingsStoriesEnabledChangedNotification (line 79-80) has no observers.
fix: Pick one key. Simplest: change TGSettingsStoriesEnabledKey (TGSettingsViewController.m:71) to @"TGShowStoriesTray" so +storiesEnabled/+setStoriesEnabled: and TGStoriesTrayEnabled() agree, and make +storiesEnabled default to YES when the key is absent (it currently defaults from `objectForKey:` with no default, line 717-719) so both sides agree on the unset case. Then have TGChatListViewController observe TGSettingsStoriesEnabledChangedNotification and rebuild its header rows.

what: The TDLib message-content -> one-line-label table is written five times with divergent output: TGMessagePreview (TGClient.m:1628-1679), TGSearchPreview (TGClient+Search.m:17-38), TGForumsPreview (TGClient+Forums.m:25-38), TGSavedPreview (TGClient+SavedMessages.m:37-49), -quoteKindLabelFor: (TGChatViewController.m:4134-4154). They disagree: messageDocument is "Document" in three copies and "File" in TGChatViewController.m:4136+ and TGClient+Notifications.m:553; messageAudio is "Audio" in four and "Music" in TGChatViewController.m:4134; messageVenue is handled only in TGClient+SavedMessages.m:47 and TGClient.m:1657. Crucially only TGClient.m's copy ignores the caption: the other four return content[@"caption"][@"text"] first (TGClient+Search.m:11-15, TGClient+Forums.m:19-24, TGClient+SavedMessages.m:28-33).
failure: Send or receive a photo with the caption "see you at 7". The chat list row (which goes through -previewForLastMessage:inChat: -> TGMessagePreview, TGClient.m:2365) shows "Photo", while the identical chat found through search shows "see you at 7". The same message therefore reads differently in two places in the app, and the chat list loses the only information that distinguishes captioned media rows from each other.
fix: Extract one function, e.g. `NSString *TGContentPreview(NSDictionary *content)`, into a shared header (TGClient+Private.h is already imported by every TGClient category). Body: caption-first (guarded isKindOfClass: on content, caption dict and caption[@"text"]), then the union of the five tables using one label per type (settle on "Document", "Audio", and add messageVenue -> "Location" and messageLiveLocation -> "Live location" everywhere), then the TGPhraseFromTypeName fallback from TGClient.m:1678. Replace all five bodies with a call to it.

what: The same four TDLib guard helpers (dict/array/string/isError) are copy-pasted 22 times under 22 different prefixes: TGDict/TGArray/TGString/TGIsError in TGClient+Contacts.m:4-25, TGClient+Groups.m:4-18 and TGClient+Stickers.m:4-27; plus prefixed clones TGAccount* (TGClient+Account.m:4-42), TGAS* (TGClient+AppSettings.m:4-21), TGB* (TGClient+Bots.m:4-22), TGCalls* (TGClient+Calls.m:4-25), TGCh* (TGClient+Channels.m:4-25), TGCM* (TGClient+ChatManagement.m:7-28), TGFiles* (TGClient+Files.m:19-34), TGMC* (TGClient+MessageContent.m:23), TGMsg* (TGClient+Messages.m:4), TGNet* (TGClient+Network.m:26-61), TGNotif* (TGClient+Notifications.m:15-33), TGPay* (TGClient+Payments.m:7), TGPremium* (TGClient+Premium.m:50-78), TGPrivacy* (TGClient+Privacy.m:4-33), TGSc* (TGClient+SecretChats.m:11-26), TGStorage* (TGClient+Storage.m:53), TGStory* (TGClient+Stories.m:4-23), TGTr* (TGClient+Translation.m:4), TGUS* (TGClient+UserStatus.m:22), TGWL* (TGClient+WebLinks.m:4).
