The contracts contradict each other for the same name: TGString returns @"" in TGClient+Contacts.m:12 and TGClient+Groups.m:12 but nil in TGClient+Stickers.m:17; TGArray returns nil in TGClient+Contacts.m:8 and TGClient+Stickers.m:9 but @[] in TGClient+Groups.m:8. The error predicates also disagree: TGAccountIsError (TGClient+Account.m:8-9) and TGNetIsError (TGClient+Network.m:30-31) return YES when @type is not an NSString, while TGChIsError (TGClient+Channels.m:8), TGTrIsError (TGClient+Translation.m:8) and TGWLIsError (TGClient+WebLinks.m:8) return NO for the same input.
failure: Any agent moving code between two of these files silently changes its behaviour. Concretely: code written against TGClient+Groups.m's contract, e.g. `for (id x in TGArray(v))`, is safe there (@[] on a bad reply) but iterates nil (no-op, silently empty result) if pasted into TGClient+Contacts.m; and `@{ @"title" : TGString(v) }` is safe in TGClient+Groups.m but throws NSInvalidArgumentException ("attempt to insert nil object") in TGClient+Stickers.m, where TGString returns nil. Every current call site in TGClient+Stickers.m happens to write `TGString(...) ?: @""` (lines 60, 97, 98, 456, 507), which is exactly the defensive tax the divergence imposes.
fix: Add one set of `static inline` helpers to src/TGClient+Private.h (already imported by all of these files) with a single documented contract: TGDict -> nil on mismatch, TGArray -> @[] on mismatch, TGString -> @"" on mismatch, TGNumber -> nil, TGInt64 -> longLongValue of NSNumber/NSString else 0, TGIsError -> YES unless the value is an NSDictionary whose @type is an NSString other than @"error". Delete all 22 prefixed copies and rename their call sites. Keep the non-generic helpers (TGNetProxyDict, TGAccountSessionDict, TGWLRichPair etc.) where they are.

what: TGActionsMenuButton (TGActionsMenu.m:26-108) is a near-verbatim copy of TGPopupMenuButton (TGPopupMenu.m:18-104): the same seven UIImageView ivars, the same four `MenuButtonTopLine.png` / `MenuButtonBottomLine.png` / `_Highlighted` loads, the same -applyHighlight:, -setHighlighted:, -setSelected: and -layoutSubviews. The three layout constants are duplicated verbatim too: `kMenuHeight = 41.0f; kMenuTitlePadding = 34.0f; kMenuLineInset = 10.0f;` at TGPopupMenu.m:4-6 and again at TGActionsMenu.m:13-15. Each file also keeps its own open-menu singleton (`static TGPopupMenu *sOpenMenu` TGPopupMenu.m:8, `static TGActionsMenuView *sOpenMenu` TGActionsMenu.m:126) and its own +dismiss.
failure: ~110 lines of pixel-layout code and three metrics exist twice, so a change to the menu card (for example the row height, which drives both the popup card and the actions menu) applied to one file leaves the other at the old value and the two menus in the same screen render at different heights. The two independent singletons also mean neither +dismiss closes the other; TGChatListViewController.m:1122-1123 only works because it happens to call both, and any new call site that calls one will leave the other's full-screen tap-catcher installed.
fix: Move TGPopupMenuButton and the three kMenu* constants into a shared internal header (e.g. TGPopupMenu+Internal.h) and have TGActionsMenu.m use TGPopupMenuButton instead of TGActionsMenuButton; delete TGActionsMenu.m:22-108 and 13-15. Then make one of the two +dismiss methods dismiss both singletons so a single call is sufficient.

what: The "first letter of the title, uppercased" avatar-initials helper is written eight times, and four of the copies index by UTF-16 unit instead of by composed character. Broken copies: `NSString *initials = title.length ? [title substringToIndex:1] : @"?";` at TGChatListViewController.m:2751, TGForwardPicker.m:627, TGStickersViewController.m:1685, TGChatViewController.m:2509, plus -initialsForName: (TGSettingsViewController.m:356-360), -initialsForTitle: (TGFoldersViewController.m:773-777) and -initialsForName: (TGInviteLinksViewController.m:599-610). Correct copies that use rangeOfComposedCharacterSequenceAtIndex:0 exist at TGCallViewController.m:182-187, TGTopicsViewController.m:72-77 and TGEventsInitials (TGChatEventsViewController.m:93-108).
failure: A chat whose title starts with an emoji or any non-BMP character (extremely common for Telegram groups and channels, e.g. "\U0001F525 Deals") hits substringToIndex:1, which cuts the surrogate pair in half. The placeholder avatar in the chat list, the forward picker and the sticker-set list draws a lone unpaired high surrogate: a blank or replacement glyph instead of a letter. The same chat drawn by TGTopicsViewController or TGCallViewController shows the emoji correctly, so the same conversation has two different placeholder avatars in the same app.
fix: Add one helper next to the drawing code it feeds, e.g. `+ (NSString *)initialsForTitle:(NSString *)title` on TGIcons (declared in TGIcons.h beside +avatarWithInitials:size:colourId:), implemented with the TGEventsInitials body from TGChatEventsViewController.m:93-108 (composed-character-sequence, up to two words, @"?" fallback). Replace all eight sites with a call to it; note TGFoldersViewController.m:775 currently falls back to @"#" and TGSettingsViewController.m:358 to @"T" for the empty case, so pass those through explicitly if the difference is wanted.

what: TGDateUtils (src/TGDateUtils.mm, a port of the original 2013 client's date code) exists specifically to answer the device's 12h/24h setting - it computes value_dateHas12hFormat at TGDateUtils.mm:34 and exposes it as TGUse12hDateFormat() (TGDateUtils.mm:56-60) and +stringForShortTime:. Only three files use it (TGDateLabel.m, TGChatEventsViewController.m, TGSavedMessagesTagsViewController.m). Sixteen other files roll their own NSDateFormatter, and the message-clock ones hardcode a 24-hour pattern: `[hm setDateFormat:@"HH:mm"]` at TGChatViewController.m:4202, again at 4963 and 4989, and `[time setDateFormat:@"HH:mm"]` with an en_US_POSIX locale at TGChatListViewController.m:2165.
failure: On a device whose region/locale uses a 12-hour clock (US default), every message timestamp in a bubble (-stampFor:, TGChatViewController.m:4200) and every chat-list row younger than 24h (TGChatDate, TGChatListViewController.m:2155) reads "14:05" instead of "2:05 PM", while the pinned-message date label and the chat-events screen - which do go through TGDateUtils - correctly read "2:05 PM" on the very same screen. The en_US_POSIX locale pinned at TGChatListViewController.m:2164 makes this permanent regardless of user setting.
fix: Replace the bodies of -stampFor: (TGChatViewController.m:4200-4210), the two other HH:mm formatters (TGChatViewController.m:4963, 4989) and the `time` branch of TGChatDate (TGChatListViewController.m:2163-2171) with `[TGDateUtils stringForShortTime:(int)date]`. Keep the weekday/full formatters in TGChatDate but drop the hardcoded en_US_POSIX locale so they follow the device, or route them through +stringForDialogTime: which already implements the same today/this-week/older cascade.

what: +avatarWithInitials:size:colourId: (TGIcons.m:849-901) does a full offscreen render every call - UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions, a rounded-rect fill, a clipped ellipse highlight and a -drawAtPoint:withFont: - and unlike +iconNamed:draw: (TGIcons.m:46-84) it never touches the sCache dictionary. One caller noticed and built a private cache: -avatarForUser:name: (TGChatViewController.m:2503-2515) memoises into self.senderAvatars, with the comment at 2501 "drawing it every row would re-download and re-decode on every scroll". The other callers did not: TGChatListViewController.m:2752, TGForwardPicker.m:628, TGStickersViewController.m:1686, TGSavedMessagesViewController.m:615, TGInviteLinksViewController.m:579, TGTopicsViewController.m:988, TGSettingsViewController.m:299 and :383 all call it straight from -tableView:cellForRowAtIndexPath: or a refresh path.
failure: Scrolling the chat list on the iPhone 4S: every visible row without a downloaded photo triggers a fresh 60x60 @2x CGBitmapContext allocation, a bezier fill, a clip+ellipse and a text draw, on the main thread inside cellForRow. At ~8 visible rows and 60 reuse events per second of flick scrolling that is hundreds of offscreen contexts per second on one A5 core, which is exactly the stutter TGChatViewController.m:2501 documents avoiding.
fix: Give TGIcons a bounded cache for placeholders: key on [NSString stringWithFormat:@"av-%@-%d-%d-%d", initials, (int)size, (int)(llabs(colourId) % 7), (int)[TGTheme shared].isFlat] in an NSCache with countLimit ~64 (NSCache, not the unbounded sCache dictionary at TGIcons.m:4, so it drops under memory pressure), return the hit before the UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions at line 867, and store before the return at line 900. Then delete the now-redundant self.senderAvatars placeholder memoisation in TGChatViewController.m:2506-2513 (keep the downloaded-photo half).

what: Two producers build the 'chat summary' dictionary that the UI consumes, with contradictory conventions and disjoint key sets. TGClient.m:2305-2308 sets only `info[@"isGroup"] = @(![chatType isEqualToString:@"chatTypePrivate"] && ![chatType isEqualToString:@"chatTypeSecret"])` - so a channel is isGroup=YES - and never writes @"isChannel" or @"isPrivate" at all. -tgs_summaryForChat: (TGClient+Search.m:362-401) sets isGroup=NO for a channel (line 371-373) and writes isChannel and isPrivate as separate keys (lines 393-395).
failure: TGSearchViewController's chat-type tabs filter on all three keys (TGSearchViewController.m:1639-1643: `_chatTypeIndex == 1 && ![chat[@"isPrivate"] boolValue]`, `== 2 && ![chat[@"isGroup"]...]`, `== 3 && ![chat[@"isChannel"]...]`). That filter can only ever run on rows from tgs_summaryForChat. The local-search rows built from [TGClient shared].chats at TGSearchViewController.m:1336-1346 carry no isChannel/isPrivate key at all and use the opposite isGroup meaning, and -runLocalSearch applies no _chatTypeIndex check anywhere. Result: with the "Channels" or "Private Chats" tab selected, every locally-matching chat of every type still appears in the chat-hits section, while the server results below it are filtered correctly.
fix: Make TGClient.m's -applyChat: write the same three keys as tgs_summaryForChat: replace lines 2305-2308 with isPrivate = (chatTypePrivate || chatTypeSecret), isChannel = (chatTypeSupergroup && type[@"is_channel"] boolValue), isGroup = (chatTypeBasicGroup || (chatTypeSupergroup && !isChannel)); check every existing reader of @"isGroup" that relied on channels being grouped in (TGChatListViewController.m:2729, 2788, 2871, 2928; AppDelegate.m:316, 437; TGForwardPicker.m:653) and change them to `isGroup || isChannel` where the old meaning was intended. Then apply the same _chatTypeIndex filter from lines 1639-1643 inside -runLocalSearch's loop (TGSearchViewController.m:1336).

what: Four independent byte/megabyte formatters with four different thresholds and precisions: TGHumanSize (TGStorageViewController.m:267-275) does "%.0f KB"/"%.1f MB"/"%.2f GB" from bytes; TGMediaViewController.m:44-50 does "%.0f KB"/"%.1f MB"/"%.2f GB" from bytes with its own thresholds; TGDeviceViewController.m:46-48 does "%.1f GB"/"%.0f MB" from megabytes; TGPremiumViewController.m:389-391 does "%.0f GB"/"%.0f MB" from megabytes. TGSettingsViewController.m:850 formats a fifth way inline ("photos to %lld KB").
failure: The same 1536 MB limit reads "1.5 GB" on the Device screen and "2 GB" on the Premium screen (%.0f rounds up), and the same 1,572,864-byte file reads "1.5 MB" in Storage and "1.5 MB" in Media but "1536 KB" in Settings. Nothing crashes; the numbers shown to the user for one quantity disagree between screens.
fix: Promote TGHumanSize(long long bytes) from TGStorageViewController.m:267 to a shared function (declare it in TGIcons.h or a small TGFormat.h) and add a `TGHumanSizeFromMegabytes(long long mb)` wrapper that calls it with mb * 1024 * 1024. Replace TGMediaViewController.m:44-50, TGDeviceViewController.m:46-48, TGPremiumViewController.m:389-391 and TGSettingsViewController.m:850 with calls to those two.

what: TGMessagePreview tests the same content type twice: `if ([ctype isEqualToString:@"messageVideoNote"]) return @"Video message";` appears at line 1640-1641 and identically again at line 1650-1651. The second copy is unreachable.
failure: No runtime failure - the first branch always wins - but the duplicate is the fingerprint of the copy-paste that produced the five divergent preview tables, and it costs a string comparison on the hot chat-list rebuild path for every non-video-note message that falls through to it.
fix: Delete TGClient.m lines 1650-1651.

what: `@"emojiId" : fullType[@"custom_emoji_id"] ?: @(0)` stores the raw JSON value. `custom_emoji_id` is int64 in td_api.tl (stickerFullTypeCustomEmoji), and td_json_client encodes every int64 field as a JSON string, so this key holds an NSString, not the NSNumber the header (TGClient+Forums.h:170) promises. Same raw pass-through at TGClient+Forums.m:86 for `icon[@"custom_emoji_id"]` -> @"iconEmojiId".
failure: TGTopicsViewController.m:57 `TGTopicLongLong` returns `[value isKindOfClass:[NSNumber class]] ? [value longLongValue] : 0`. At TGTopicsViewController.m:1507 it reads @"emojiId" from a -forumTopicDefaultIconsWithCompletion: entry, gets an NSString, and yields 0. That 0 flows through commitCreateWithName:iconEmojiId: / commitEditWithName:changeIcon:iconEmojiId: into TGClient+Forums.m:256 `@"custom_emoji_id" : @(iconEmojiId)` and :283 `@"icon_custom_emoji_id" : @(...)`. Result: the user picks a topic icon emoji in the action sheet and the topic is always created/edited with no custom emoji icon at all, falling back to the colour circle. Silent, never logged.

what: `topic[@"order"] ?: @(0)` passes forumTopic.order straight through. Per td_api.tl:3926 `forumTopic ... order:int64`, so this is a JSON string, while TGClient+Forums.h:45 documents `"order" NSNumber int64 sort order`. TGClient.m:1682-1689 already documents and handles exactly this trap for chatPosition.order ('It is an int64 sent as a string, so it must not be compared as a string').
failure: No caller currently sorts on this key (grep for "order" in TGTopicsViewController.m returns nothing), so there is no live failure today. The next caller that follows the header and does `[topic[@"order"] compare:...]` as NSNumber, or `isEqualToNumber:`, gets either a wrong ordering or an unrecognized-selector crash on the NSString.
fix: Wrap with the same TGForumsInt64 helper: `TGForumsInt64(topic[@"order"]), @"order",` at TGClient+Forums.m:88.

what: `topicId, @"topicId", topicId, @"threadId",` aliases forum_topic_id (int32, td_api.tl:3911) to the key "threadId", which TGClient+Messages.m:13-17 TGMsgTopic feeds into `messageTopicThread message_thread_id:int53` (td_api.tl:2983). TGClient+Forums.h:6-9 itself flags that these are not the same identifier.
failure: TGTopicsViewController.m:1023-1030 reads @"threadId" and assigns it to the chat controller's threadId; sends into that topic build messageTopicThread with a forum_topic_id where a message_thread_id is expected. Not a width truncation (int32 widens cleanly into int53) but a wrong-namespace id: the server resolves it to a different thread or rejects it, so messages sent from a topic land outside the topic.
fix: Not a width bug; noted here because it is the only remaining id-identity problem in this area. The correct construction is `@{@"@type":@"messageTopicForum", @"forum_topic_id":@((int32_t)topicId)}` when the target chat is a forum, versus messageTopicThread for legacy comment threads. Confirm with the forums/messages owner before changing; do not simply widen the type.

what: `clean: @rm -rf "$(BUILD_DIR)"` deletes the entire build/ tree, which is not just intermediates: it also holds build/sdks (the theos SDK clone), build/{armv7,arm64}/libs (libcrypto.a, libssl.a, libwebp.a), build/{armv7,arm64}/tdlib/lib/libtdjson.dylib and build/tools/machofix.
failure: After `make clean && make ipa-armv7`, SDK_PATH's wildcard checks at lines 42-48 all miss and fall through to $(XCODE_SDK). The Makefile's own comment at lines 50-53 states that the modern Xcode SDK ships no armv7 slice in libSystem.tbd, so the armv7 link fails with undefined libc symbols. Even if an SDK is restored, -lcrypto is unresolved (build/armv7/libs gone) and the libtdjson.dylib copy at line 329 silently degrades to the `|| echo` branch, producing an app bundle with no TDLib that dlopen-fails at startup in TGClient.m:42. None of these are rebuildable by any Makefile target.
fix: Make `clean` remove only generated intermediates: `rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)/armv7/obj $(BUILD_DIR)/arm64/obj $(BUILD_DIR)/armv7/app $(BUILD_DIR)/arm64/app $(BUILD_DIR)/fat_app $(BUILD_DIR)/Payload $(IPA_DIR)`. Add a separate `distclean` target that additionally removes build/sdks, build/libs, build/*/libs, build/*/tdlib and build/tdlib-dylib-*, and document that distclean requires re-running scripts/setup_sdk.sh, scripts/build_deps.sh and scripts/build_tdlib_dylib.sh.

what: build_deps.sh writes its output to `BUILD_LIBS_DIR="${ROOT_DIR}/build/libs"` (lines 10, 30-31, 37-40), but the Makefile links against `-L$(BUILD_DIR)/armv7/libs` (Makefile:323) and `-L$(BUILD_DIR)/arm64/libs` (Makefile:343), and scripts/build_tdlib_dylib.sh:84-85 reads build/armv7/libs/libcrypto.a. Nothing populates the per-arch directories.
failure: On a fresh clone the documented dependency bootstrap produces build/libs/libcrypto.a only. The armv7 link then fails with `ld: library not found for -lcrypto` (DEPS_LIBS, Makefile:95), and build_tdlib_dylib.sh's cmake configure fails because OPENSSL_CRYPTO_LIBRARY points at a nonexistent path. The current tree only works because build/armv7/libs and build/arm64/libs were populated by hand at some point.
fix: In scripts/build_deps.sh, extract per-architecture slices into the directories the build actually uses: create build/armv7/libs and build/arm64/libs and run `lipo <universal>.a -thin armv7 -output build/armv7/libs/libcrypto.a` and `-thin arm64 -output build/arm64/libs/libcrypto.a` (same for libssl, libwebp), instead of a single dual-arch archive in build/libs. Also fix scripts/build_tdlib.sh:97-98, which still reads the old build/libs path.

what: README documents `make app`, `make deps` and `make tdlib` (README.md:86-88). The Makefile's only targets are `all ipa ipa-armv7 ipa-arm64 clean help` (.PHONY, Makefile:292) plus the object and $(MACHOFIX) rules.
failure: A new contributor following the README runs `make deps` and gets `make: *** No rule to make target 'deps'.  Stop.`, then runs `make` and hits the missing -lcrypto link error from the previous finding. The documented bootstrap path does not exist.
fix: Either add the targets — `deps: ; @scripts/build_deps.sh`, `tdlib: ; @scripts/build_tdlib_dylib.sh && scripts/build_tdlib_dylib_arm64.sh`, and drop `app` — adding them to .PHONY on Makefile:292, or correct README.md:86-88 to reference the scripts directly (scripts/setup_sdk.sh, scripts/build_deps.sh, scripts/build_tdlib_dylib.sh).

what: `ipa: ipa-armv7 ipa-arm64` — both prerequisites use the same shared staging directory: ipa-armv7 does `rm -rf "$(BUILD_DIR)/Payload"` / `mkdir` / `cp` / `cd $(BUILD_DIR) && zip -qr` (lines 333-337) and ipa-arm64 does the identical sequence on the same path (lines 348-352). The `ipa` recipe itself reuses it again at lines 302-306.
failure: With `make -j2 ipa` (or any -j, which is the natural way to build 88k lines on a laptop) the two arch targets interleave: ipa-arm64 can `rm -rf build/Payload` while ipa-armv7 is mid-`zip`, yielding a truncated or empty iTgLegacy-armv7.ipa, or zip picking up the arm64 bundle so the armv7 IPA contains an arm64 binary that will not launch on the 4S. The failure is nondeterministic and silent — zip -q reports nothing.
fix: Give each target its own staging dir: use `$(BUILD_DIR)/Payload-armv7` in the ipa-armv7 recipe (lines 333-337), `$(BUILD_DIR)/Payload-arm64` in ipa-arm64 (lines 348-352), and `$(BUILD_DIR)/Payload-fat` in ipa (lines 302-306), each with a matching `mv`/`rm` of only its own directory, and zip with `cd $(BUILD_DIR)/stage-<arch>`.

what: No compilation rule emits or includes header dependencies: every rule is a bare `$(CC) $(FLAGS) -c $< -o $@` with no `-MMD -MP` and no `-include $(OBJS:.o=.d)` anywhere in the file.
failure: Editing any header — e.g. adding a field to a struct in src/TGClient.h, which ~30 TGClient+*.m files import — rebuilds nothing. The stale .o files keep the old struct layout while newly compiled ones use the new one, so the linked binary reads fields at the wrong offsets and crashes or corrupts data at runtime with no build error. In a repo where dozens of files share a handful of headers this misfires constantly, and the usual workaround (`make clean`) triggers the first finding above.
fix: Add `-MMD -MP` to CFLAGS_ARMV7 (line 279) and CFLAGS_ARM64 (line 284) so it propagates to the OBJC/CXX variants, and before the `clean` target add `-include $(ARMV7_ALL_OBJS:.o=.d)` and `-include $(ARM64_ALL_OBJS:.o=.d)`.

what: src/ChatViewCell.m (81 lines) and src/TGActionTableView.m (257 lines) exist in src/ but appear in no *_SRC_* list in the Makefile, and neither `ChatViewCell` nor `TGActionTableView` is referenced from any other file in src/ — the only hits are their own headers. src/ChatViewCell.h:3 also `#import "TGMessage.h"`, a header that does not exist anywhere in the tree.
failure: 338 lines of never-compiled code that no build error protects. Anyone who adds src/ChatViewCell.m to APP_SRC_M gets an immediate `'TGMessage.h' file not found`, and TGActionTableView.m:7 has its TGHacks import commented out, so both are unverified against the current codebase. Meanwhile grep-driven agents keep finding these classes and assuming they are live.
fix: Delete src/ChatViewCell.{m,h} and src/TGActionTableView.{m,h}. If TGActionTableView is intended for future use, add it to APP_SRC_M (Makefile:142-241) so it is at least compiled and kept honest; ChatViewCell cannot be revived without a TGMessage.h that no longer exists.

what: The generic `.mm` rules — `$(ARMV7_OBJ_DIR)/%.o: %.mm` (line 369) and `$(ARM64_OBJ_DIR)/%.o: %.mm` (line 392) — apply `$(VOIP_FLAGS)`, which is `-DTGVOIP_NO_DSP -DWEBRTC_POSIX -DTGVOIP_USE_CUSTOM_CRYPTO -I.../libtgvoip -Wno-everything` (line 135-136). VOIP_SRC_MM (line 130-133) contains src/TGCall.mm and src/TGDateUtils.mm, which are app code, not vendored libtgvoip.
failure: `-Wno-everything` disables every diagnostic for src/TGCall.mm and src/TGDateUtils.mm, including -Wobjc-method-access, -Wincompatible-pointer-types and -Wformat. A wrong selector or a %d format against an int64 chat id in TGCall.mm compiles completely silently and only shows up as a runtime crash or truncated id on the 4S. The blanket suppression is meant for the vendored public-domain C++, not for first-party ObjC++.
fix: Split the rules: keep the VOIP_FLAGS rule scoped to the vendored tree with a pattern `$(ARMV7_OBJ_DIR)/src/libtgvoip/%.o: src/libtgvoip/%.mm` (mirroring the existing .cpp rule at line 365), and give the generic `%.mm` rule the libtgvoip include and defines but drop `-Wno-everything`, e.g. compile src/TGCall.mm and src/TGDateUtils.mm with `$(CXXFLAGS_ARMV7) -I$(ROOT_DIR)/src/libtgvoip -DTGVOIP_NO_DSP -DTGVOIP_USE_CUSTOM_CRYPTO -fobjc-arc`. Same for the arm64 pair at lines 388-394.

what: WebPDecodeRGBAInto() produces straight (unpremultiplied) RGBA, but the CGImage is created declaring premultiplied alpha: `kCGBitmapByteOrderDefault | kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast`.
failure: Every WebP sticker with transparency renders wrong. CoreGraphics assumes R/G/B are already scaled by A, so it does not multiply again: a pixel of (255,255,255,64) draws as near-opaque white at 25% coverage instead of a faint white, producing bright halos around every antialiased sticker edge and colored fringes wherever the encoder left non-zero RGB under alpha=0. Fully opaque stickers look fine, which is why it survives a smoke test.
fix: Either (a) change the bitmapInfo to `kCGBitmapByteOrderDefault | kCGImageAlphaLast` (CGImage supports 8bpc straight-alpha RGBA), or (b) keep kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast and premultiply in place right after the WebPDecodeRGBAInto call, before CGDataProviderCreateWithData: loop over `size/4` pixels doing `a = pixels[i*4+3]; pixels[i*4+0] = pixels[i*4+0]*a/255;` for the three colour channels. (a) is cheaper on an A5; (b) is faster to composite. Do not do both.

what: Unguarded `isEqualToString:` on an arbitrary JSON value: `if ([item isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class] && [item[@"ty"] isEqualToString:@"tr"])`. The same file guards the identical lookup correctly 13 lines earlier (line 418-420: `NSString *ty = shape[@"ty"]; if (![ty isKindOfClass:NSString.class]) continue;`).
failure: A .tgs whose group item carries a numeric or null `ty` (hand-authored or truncated/corrupt sticker download) makes `item[@"ty"]` an NSNumber or NSNull, neither of which implements isEqualToString:. Result: `-[__NSCFNumber isEqualToString:]: unrecognized selector sent to instance` and the app terminates while scrolling a sticker into view. TGLottieView.loadTGSFile guards the top-level shape of the JSON but nothing validates group-item contents.
fix: In TGLottieView.m:429-432 replace the inline test with the same guarded form used at 418-420: `for (NSDictionary *item in items){ if (![item isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class]) continue; id ity = item[@"ty"]; if ([ity isKindOfClass:NSString.class] && [ity isEqualToString:@"tr"]) [self applyTransform:item atFrame:frame inContext:ctx]; }`.

what: TGActionsMenu.m is a near-verbatim fork of TGPopupMenu.m. TGActionsMenuButton (lines 26-112) duplicates TGPopupMenuButton (TGPopupMenu.m:18-105) field for field; -positionCard/-buttonContainsArrow/-menuButtonHighlightChanged/-layoutCard/-present (lines 431-593) duplicate TGPopupMenu.m:373-536 line for line, down to the same `kMenuHeight = 41.0f`, `kMenuTitlePadding = 34.0f`, `kMenuLineInset = 10.0f` constants, the same 0.142/0.08/0.06 three-stage bounce, and the same `shadowHighlighted = 0x18/0x6b/0xcb alpha 0.6` colour literal. ~450 duplicated lines.
failure: They have already drifted: TGActionsMenu.m:424-425 does `[_card bringSubviewToFront:_arrowTopView/_arrowBottomView]` after building buttons, TGPopupMenu.m never does (see the z-order finding below), so the two menus draw the arrow differently. Any future fix to menu geometry, hit-testing or the reopen-suppression behaviour has to be applied twice and will be applied once.
fix: Extract the shared button class and the card geometry into one place: rename TGPopupMenuButton to TGMenuCardButton in a new src/TGMenuCard.{h,m} together with positionCardIn:anchor:, buttonContainsArrow:atIndex:, layoutCardWithButtons:separators:arrowTop:arrowBottom:, and presentCard:. Have TGPopupMenu and TGActionsMenuView both call into it; delete TGActionsMenu.m:26-112 and 431-556 and TGPopupMenu.m:18-105 and 373-501.

what: TGDateUtils is the project's date formatter and it detects 12-hour locales (`value_dateHas12hFormat`, line 34), but three list screens each carry their own private copy of the same today/weekday/absolute ladder with a hardcoded 24-hour format: TGChatListViewController.m:2161-2170, TGSavedMessagesViewController.m:39-41, TGTopicsViewController.m:36-44 (`[time setDateFormat:@"HH:mm"]; [weekday setDateFormat:@"EEE"]; [full setDateFormat:@"dd.MM.yy"]`).
failure: On a US-locale iPhone 4S the chat list, saved messages and topics rows show `14:32` while the chat event log (which goes through `[TGDateUtils stringForShortTime:]`, TGChatEventsViewController.m:1113) shows `2:32 PM`, and TGDateLabel (TGDateLabel.m:40) is meanwhile stripping an " AM"/" PM" suffix that the list formatters never produce, so its two-font AM/PM rendering path is dead on exactly those screens. Two files disagree about the shape of the same value.
fix: Delete the three private static formatter trios and route all four call sites through TGDateUtils: `stringForMessageListDate:` already implements exactly this ladder (same-day -> stringForShortTime, within 6 days -> weekdayNameShort, else shortAbsoluteDate). Replace e.g. TGChatListViewController.m:2168-2170 with `return [TGDateUtils stringForMessageListDate:(int)unix];` and the same in TGSavedMessagesViewController.m and TGTopicsViewController.m.

what: Only two of the nine TGDateUtils class methods have a caller anywhere in src/: stringForShortTime: (TGChatEventsViewController.m:1113) and stringForMessageListDate: (TGSavedMessagesTagsViewController.m:130). stringForDialogTime:, stringForDayOfMonth:dayOfMonth:, stringForDayOfWeek:, stringForLastSeen:, stringForLastSeenShort:, stringForRelativeLastSeen: and stringForUntil: have zero callers. Worse, stringForDialogTime: (lines 112-120) is degenerate — the `if (dialogTimeMonthNameFirst())` branch and the fall-through return are byte-identical, and `value_dialogTimeMonthNameFirst` (line 13) is initialised false and never assigned anywhere, so the accessor at 79-83 is a constant. stringForLastSeenShort: (183-185) is a pure alias that just calls stringForLastSeen:.
failure: No runtime failure - it is ~110 lines of unreachable code plus five unread globals (value_dialogTimeMonthNameFirst, value_dialogTimeFormat, value_today/yesterday/tomorrow/at are only read from dead paths except value_today/value_yesterday). The concrete cost is that stringForLastSeen/stringForRelativeLastSeen look like the app's last-seen formatter but the real one is TGClient+UserStatus.m:30-61, so an agent fixing a last-seen bug edits the dead copy and nothing changes.
fix: Delete stringForDialogTime:, stringForDayOfMonth:dayOfMonth:, stringForDayOfWeek:, stringForLastSeenShort:, stringForRelativeLastSeen: and stringForUntil: from TGDateUtils.mm and their declarations from TGDateUtils.h, along with value_dialogTimeMonthNameFirst/value_dialogTimeFormat/dialogTimeMonthNameFirst()/dialogTimeFormat() and value_tomorrow. Keep stringForShortTime:, stringForMessageListDate:, stringForLastSeen: (needed by stringForMessageListDate's siblings if the duplication fix above lands), weekdayNameShort/monthNameGenShort/shortAbsoluteDate and TGUse12hDateFormat().

what: _arrowTopView and _arrowBottomView are added to _card at lines 247 and 252, before the buttons are added at line 355, and are never raised afterwards - unlike the equivalent code in TGActionsMenu.m:424-425 which does `[_card bringSubviewToFront:_arrowTopView]; [_card bringSubviewToFront:_arrowBottomView];` right after the button loop.
failure: The bottom arrow is positioned at y = kMenuHeight - 4 = 37 (line 463), i.e. its top 4 points overlap the button row (0..41), and the buttons are later siblings so they paint over it. TGPopupMenu's positioning prefers placing the card above the anchor (positionCardFromRect:, line 384-395 sets _arrowOnTop = NO in the common case), so the bottom arrow is the one normally visible: it renders with its top 4px clipped by the button plate, showing a hairline seam between the card and the tail on every long-press menu.
fix: In TGPopupMenu.m, after the button-building loop ends at line 363 and before `CGRect cardFrame = _card.frame;` at 365, add `[_card bringSubviewToFront:_arrowTopView]; [_card bringSubviewToFront:_arrowBottomView];` - matching TGActionsMenu.m:424-425.

what: The fill-rule branch contradicts both the Lottie spec and its own comment: `// Lottie fills use even-odd, which is what makes holes work.` then `if ([shape[@"r"] intValue] == 1) CGContextFillPath(ctx); else CGContextEOFillPath(ctx);`. In Lottie, `r` is the fill rule where 1 = non-zero and 2 = even-odd, and the value is optional with non-zero as the default.
failure: The r==1 mapping is right, but the default is wrong: when a fill item omits `r`, `[nil intValue]` is 0, so the shape is filled even-odd instead of non-zero. Any sticker whose overlapping subpaths wind in the same direction (a common result of boolean-unioned shapes) renders with holes punched where the subpaths overlap - a mouth or eye that should be solid comes out hollow.
fix: Read the value explicitly and default to non-zero: `id rule = shape[@"r"]; if ([rule intValue] == 2) CGContextEOFillPath(ctx); else CGContextFillPath(ctx);`, and correct the comment above line 566 to say Lottie defaults to non-zero and only uses even-odd when r == 2.

what: Both arms of an if/else assign the same value: `if (frame.origin.y < 2.0f){ frame.origin.y = floorf(...); _arrowOnTop = NO; } else { _arrowOnTop = NO; }` (lines 444-449).
failure: No wrong behaviour today - the value is correct in both cases - but the branch reads as if the centred fallback and the above-anchor placement are meant to differ, so an agent reading it assumes the arrow orientation is already handled for the centred case and does not notice that when the card is centred (neither above nor below the anchor) the downward arrow still points at nothing.
fix: Collapse to `if (frame.origin.y < 2.0f) frame.origin.y = floorf((self.bounds.size.height - frame.size.height) / 2); _arrowOnTop = NO;` and, if the centred case should hide the tail entirely, set a flag there and force both `_arrowTopView.hidden` and `_arrowBottomView.hidden` to YES at the end of layoutCard (lines 554-555).

what: The initialiser mutates the caller's model objects: `if (hasDestructive) action.type = TGActionSheetActionTypeGeneric;` (line 75) and `cancelAction.title = TGActionSheetCancelTitle();` (line 89) write through into the TGActionSheetAction instances the caller supplied in its `actions` array.
failure: Callers that build the array once and re-show it lose styling permanently. TGInviteLinksViewController.m:754-767 rebuilds its array each time so it is safe, but TGStoriesViewController.m:1840-1878 and TGReactionPickerView.m:1504-1519 add two destructive entries to one array (e.g. Delete plus Decline); the second is downgraded to Generic on first show and stays Generic, so on every subsequent presentation neither the caller nor the sheet can restore the red styling.
fix: Do not mutate the input. In TGActionSheet.m:72-78 track the downgrade locally (e.g. `TGActionSheetActionType effectiveType = (action.type == TGActionSheetActionTypeDestructive && hasDestructive) ? TGActionSheetActionTypeGeneric : action.type;`) and store the pair in the internal `_actions` array as a copied TGActionSheetAction, and at line 89 build a fresh cancel TGActionSheetAction rather than retitling the caller's.

what: `for (NSDictionary *layer in [[self.layers reverseObjectEnumerator] allObjects])` allocates a full reversed copy of the layer array inside drawRect:, which the 20 Hz timer (line 248) drives.
failure: On an A5 with 40-60MB usable this churns 20 autoreleased NSArrays per second per visible animated sticker, on the main thread, on top of the per-frame path building. With several .tgs stickers on screen in a chat it is measurable main-thread allocator pressure for no benefit, since the reversal is over an array that never changes after loadTGSFile:.
fix: Store the reversed order once. In loadTGSFile: after `self.layers = layers;` (line 215) also set a `_drawOrder` ivar to `[[layers reverseObjectEnumerator] allObjects]`, and iterate `_drawOrder` at line 307. Clear it alongside self.layers at lines 164-165.

what: Lazy init is unsynchronised: `static bool TGDateUtilsInitialized = false;` plus `if (!TGDateUtilsInitialized) initializeTGDateUtils();` repeated in six accessors (lines 51, 57, 63, 72, 80, 86). TGAlertView.m:7 solves the identical problem with dispatch_once.
failure: Two threads entering simultaneously both run initializeTGDateUtils(), which allocates an NSDateFormatter and writes value_dateHas12hFormat, value_date_separator and value_monthFirst. The formatter work is duplicated and a caller can read a half-initialised value_date_separator (set at 38/40/42) before value_monthFirst is computed at 44-45, producing one date string with the wrong separator or wrong field order. Rare, but the call sites do reach background queues via the image/thumbnail decode paths.
fix: Wrap the body: give initializeTGDateUtils a `static dispatch_once_t once; dispatch_once(&once, ^{ ... });` around lines 26-47, and drop the TGDateUtilsInitialized flag and the six `if (!TGDateUtilsInitialized)` guards in favour of an unconditional call to initializeTGDateUtils() at the top of each accessor.

what: `NSDictionary *status = TGUserStatusInfo(obj[@"status"]);` is called at line 351 but the function is only defined at line 555 (`static NSDictionary *TGUserStatusInfo(...)`); the same pattern exists for `text = TGMessagePreview(m);` at line 877 vs. its definition at line 1628. Only `TGFlattenMessage` has a forward declaration (line 9). The Makefile builds with `-Wno-implicit-function-declaration` (Makefile:280/285), so this compiles silently.
failure: With no visible prototype clang codegens the call against the implicit signature `int f()`. On the armv7 slice the 32-bit return in r0 happens to alias the pointer, so it works by accident. On the arm64 slice (build/arm64/obj/src/TGClient.o is built by the same Makefile) the return value is truncated to a 32-bit int and sign-extended, so `status` / `text` is a garbage pointer: the very next `status[@"isOnline"]` (line 360) or `text.length` (line 884) messages a wild address and crashes with EXC_BAD_ACCESS on the first updateUserStatus / on every non-text message.
fix: Next to the existing forward declaration at TGClient.m:9 add `static NSDictionary *TGUserStatusInfo(NSDictionary *status);` and `static NSString *TGMessagePreview(NSDictionary *message);`. Do not rely on -Wno-implicit-function-declaration to keep hiding it.

what: `obj[@"usernames"][@"active_usernames"][0]` indexes element 0 of a TDLib array with no count check. Same unguarded `[0]` at lines 205 (`updateUser`), 1365 (`contactsWithCompletion:`), 1428 (`userForPhone:`) and 2267 (`ensureUserName:`).
failure: td_api's `usernames` object is `active_usernames:vector<string> disabled_usernames:vector<string> editable_username:string`. A user who owns a username but has it disabled gets a non-nil `usernames` object with an EMPTY `active_usernames` array. `array[0]` then goes through -objectAtIndexedSubscript: and raises NSRangeException, which is uncaught on the main queue. At line 193 this happens on the getMe reply, i.e. the app terminates during login for such an account; at line 205 any `updateUser` for such a contact kills the app mid-session.
fix: Replace every `x[@"usernames"][@"active_usernames"][0]` with a guarded helper, e.g. add `static NSString *TGFirstUsername(NSDictionary *u){ NSArray *a = u[@"usernames"][@"active_usernames"]; return ([a isKindOfClass:NSArray.class] && a.count && [a[0] isKindOfClass:NSString.class]) ? a[0] : nil; }` and call it at 193, 205, 1365, 1428, 2267.

what: `-forumTopicsForChat:completion:` reads the topic id as `info[@"message_thread_id"]` and pages with `@"offset_message_thread_id" : @(0)` (line 1898). td_api.tl:3911 says `forumTopicInfo chat_id:int53 forum_topic_id:int32 ...` — there is no `message_thread_id` field — and td_api.tl:12510 says `getForumTopics ... offset_forum_topic_id:int32 ...`.
failure: `info[@"message_thread_id"]` is always nil, so every returned topic carries `@"threadId" : @(0)`. Any caller opening a topic with that id would send `message_thread_id: 0` and land in the merged chat stream instead of the topic, and paging would restart from the top forever. The request field `offset_message_thread_id` is also unknown to this TDLib and is ignored.
fix: Either delete this method (see the dead-code finding — TGTopicsViewController.m:781/863 use TGClient+Forums.m's `-forumTopicsForChat:query:offsetDate:offsetMessageId:offsetTopicId:limit:completion:` instead), or change line 1906 to `info[@"forum_topic_id"]` and line 1898 to `@"offset_forum_topic_id" : @(0)`. If deleted, also remove the declaration at TGClient.h:99.

what: `-premiumStateWithCompletion:` gates on `if (![me[@"is_premium"] boolValue]) { completion(nil); return; }`, but `self.me` is constructed at lines 190-195 with exactly four keys: `id`, `first_name`, `username`, `phone`. It never contains `is_premium`. The line below (1481) also reads `state[@"state"][@"expiration_date"]`, while td_api.tl:8166 declares `premiumState state:formattedText ...` — a formattedText has no `expiration_date`.
failure: The completion is unconditionally called with nil for every account, premium or not, so the premium row never appears; even if the guard were removed, the expiry lookup would always miss and the answer would be the bare string "Active".
fix: Add `@"is_premium" : obj[@"is_premium"] ?: @NO` (and `@"last_name"`) to the `self.me` dictionary built at TGClient.m:190, and take the expiry from the account's own `getUserFullInfo` / `premium_expiration_date` option rather than from `premiumState`, which only carries promo text. The same stale `self.me[@"is_premium"]` read exists at TGClient+Premium.m:168.

what: In `-chatProfile:completion:` the shared `answer` block does `@"members" : full[@"member_count"] ?: @0;` and it is used for both supergroups (line 1959) and basic groups (line 1963). td_api.tl:2696 `basicGroupFullInfo photo description creator_user_id members:vector<chatMember> ...` has no `member_count` field.
failure: Opening the profile of a plain (non-super) group shows "0 members" no matter how many members it has, because `full[@"member_count"]` is nil for basicGroupFullInfo.
fix: In the `answer` block use `@"members" : full[@"member_count"] ?: @([full[@"members"] count])`, or pass the count in from each branch: supergroups from `member_count`, basic groups from `[full[@"members"] count]`.

what: `-applyChatUpdate:` handling a single-list `updateChatPosition`: the archive branch does `info[@"archiveOrder"] = ...; info[@"order"] = @(0);` and the main branch (line 2418) does `info[@"archiveOrder"] = @(0);`. One list's position update clobbers the order the chat holds in the other list.
failure: TDLib removes a chat from a list by sending updateChatPosition for that list with order "0". When a chat lives in the archive and TDLib emits the chatListMain removal (order 0), line 2416-2418 sets order=0 AND archiveOrder=0; `-rebuildChats` (2440-2443) then puts the chat in neither `chats` nor `archivedChats`, so an archived chat silently vanishes from the archive until an unrelated full `updateNewChat` re-seeds it.
fix: Only write the field that belongs to the list named in `position[@"list"][@"@type"]`: in the chatListArchive branch set `archiveOrder` only, in the chatListMain branch set `order` and `isPinned` only. Drop both `= @(0)` clobbers at lines 2415 and 2418.

what: `-statusForUser:completion:` decides "today" with `BOOL today = [[NSCalendar currentCalendar] components:NSDayCalendarUnit fromDate:date].day == [[NSCalendar currentCalendar] components:NSDayCalendarUnit fromDate:[NSDate date]].day;` — that is the day-of-month only, with no month or year.
failure: A user last seen at 12:30 on 14 July, viewed on 14 August, reads "last seen at 12:30" as if they were online this morning. Any last-seen whose day-of-month happens to match today is mis-labelled; everything else collapses to "last seen a long time ago", so a yesterday-evening status also reads as "a long time ago".
fix: Delete the whole body of -statusForUser:completion: and implement it as `if (completion) completion(TGUserStatusInfo(user[@"status"])[@"text"]);` — TGUserStatusInfo (TGClient.m:555) already computes today/yesterday/weekday/date correctly from full year+month+day components.

what: The last-seen phrase is written three times: `TGUserStatusInfo` (TGClient.m:555), `-statusForUser:completion:` (TGClient.m:1719, a worse copy — see the previous finding), and `TGUSLastSeenText` (TGClient+UserStatus.m:35). All three produce different strings for the same input: TGClient.m:579 gives "last seen today at 12:30" while TGClient.m:1747 gives "last seen at 12:30" and TGUSLastSeenText gives "last seen today at 12:30" but with a different long-ago fallback.
failure: The same user shows a different subtitle in the chat header (statusForUser:), the chat list (TGUserStatusInfo via updateUserStatus) and the profile (TGClient+UserStatus.m), and a fix applied to one is invisible in the other two.
fix: Keep one implementation. Promote `TGUserStatusInfo` out of TGClient.m into TGClient+Private.h as an exported `NSDictionary *TGUserStatusInfo(NSDictionary *status)`, make -statusForUser:completion: return `TGUserStatusInfo(...)[@"text"]`, and have TGClient+UserStatus.m's TGUSLastSeenText call it instead of re-deriving the text.

what: `self.pendingRequests[extra] = [completion copy];` in `-request:completion:`. Entries are removed only in -handleUpdate: (line 167) when a reply carrying the matching `@extra` arrives. There is no timeout, no purge on authorizationStateClosed, and no purge when `-start` fails.
failure: When TDLib never answers — dlopen failed so `available` is NO and drainOutbox (line 133) drops nothing but never sends, or the client was closed by logOut (line 426 sets running=NO and the receive loop exits) — the completion block is retained forever and never invoked. Any screen that shows a spinner until its completion fires (e.g. TGStorageViewController's -storageStatsWithCompletion:, TGProfileViewController's -userProfile:) spins for the life of the process, and every captured view controller stays alive with it.
fix: Give -request:completion: a timeout: store `@{ @"block": [completion copy], @"deadline": @(CFAbsoluteTimeGetCurrent() + 30) }`, and from -receiveLoop (or a 5 s main-queue timer) sweep expired entries, invoking each with `@{@"@type":@"error", @"code":@(-1), @"message":@"timeout"}`. Also flush and error out every pending request in -handleAuthState: when the state is authorizationStateClosed, and in -start when it returns NO.

what: `NSString *extra = [NSString stringWithFormat:@"r%lu", (unsigned long)(++self.requestSeq)];` followed by `self.pendingRequests[extra] = [completion copy];` — both run on whatever thread called -request:, while -handleUpdate: reads and mutates the same NSMutableDictionary on the main queue (lines 165-167). Neither `requestSeq` nor `pendingRequests` is protected (the only lock in the class, `outboxLock`, guards the outbox only).
failure: -request: is reachable from background queues (callers such as TGChatViewController.m:3934 and TGProfileViewController.m:2046 hop to a global queue before touching the client). Two concurrent `++self.requestSeq` on a non-atomic NSUInteger property can produce the same @extra, so one caller's completion overwrites the other's and one screen never gets its reply; concurrent -setObject:forKey: against the main thread's -removeObjectForKey: can corrupt the CFDictionary's bucket array and crash in CFBasicHashAddValue.
fix: Serialise both: either wrap lines 151-152 and 165-167 in a dedicated NSLock (mirroring outboxLock), or make -request:completion: enqueue its bookkeeping with `dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue(), ...)` so the seq bump, the dictionary insert and the handleUpdate lookup all happen on the main queue.

what: Nine public methods declared in TGClient.h and implemented in TGClient.m have no caller anywhere outside TGClient.m/TGClient.h: -sessionsWithCompletion: (1537), -terminateSession: (1555, TGSessionsViewController.m:503 calls the category's -terminateSession:completion: instead), -setName:last: (1559), -premiumStateWithCompletion: (1473), -chatsInFolder:completion: (1865), -userForPhone:completion: (1410), -setUser:blocked: (1437), -notificationsMutedForScope:completion: + -setScope:muted: (2004/2015), -setChat:joined: (1841), and -forumTopicsForChat:completion: (1891). Two declared ivars are also unused: `fileWaiters` is allocated at line 27 and never read or written again anywhere in the tree, and `chatsAtLastLoad` is written at line 1596 and never read.
failure: No runtime failure, but roughly 150 lines of TGClient.m are unreachable, three of them (forumTopicsForChat:completion:, premiumStateWithCompletion:, chatProfile: for basic groups) are actively wrong against the current td_api.tl, and a future caller wiring them up would inherit those bugs. `fileWaiters` in particular reads as live download plumbing that does not exist.
fix: Delete the ten methods and their TGClient.h declarations, and remove the `fileWaiters` and `chatsAtLastLoad` properties from TGClient+Private.h (lines 36 and 43) plus the `s.fileWaiters = ...` line at TGClient.m:27 and the write at TGClient.m:1596. Keep -terminateSession: only if TGClient+Account.m's variant is removed instead.

what: `-isUserBlocked:completion:` answers `completion([full[@"block_list"] isKindOfClass:NSDictionary.class]);` — any non-null BlockList counts as blocked.
failure: td_api has two block lists, `blockListMain` and `blockListStories`. A user muted only from stories comes back with `block_list: {"@type":"blockListStories"}`, so the profile shows "Unblock" for someone who is not actually blocked, and tapping it sends setMessageSenderBlockList with a null list, silently un-restricting their stories instead.
fix: Change the test to `completion([full[@"block_list"][@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"blockListMain"]);`.

what: `TGMessagePreview` tests `messageVideoNote` twice: line 1640 `if ([ctype isEqualToString:@"messageVideoNote"]) return @"Video message";` and again at line 1650 with the identical body.
failure: The second branch is unreachable. Harmless today, but it is exactly the kind of duplicate that makes a later edit to one copy look like it had no effect.
fix: Delete lines 1650-1651.

what: +waveform:size:played:colour: opens a graphics context on line 680 and then bails out of the method without closing it: `NSUInteger bars = (NSUInteger)(size.width / (barW + gap)); if (bars == 0) return nil;` — there is no UIGraphicsEndImageContext() on that path.
failure: Any call with 0 < size.width < 3 (a voice-note wave view that has been laid out narrow, or a cell mid-animation) creates and pushes a CGBitmapContext that is never popped. The orphaned context stays on top of the UIKit context stack for the lifetime of the process, so every subsequent UIGraphicsGetCurrentContext()/UIGraphicsGetImageFromCurrentImageContext() in the app — every TGIcons glyph, every avatar in +avatarWithInitials:, every bubble tail — draws into and reads back from that stale bitmap instead of its own. Icons and avatars come back blank or wrong from that point on, and each occurrence leaks size.width*size.height*4*scale^2 bytes. -playbackTick (src/TGChatViewController.m:2948) calls this five times a second per visible cell with `bubble.wave.bounds.size`, so it only takes one narrow wave view to poison the whole drawing stack.
fix: Move the degenerate-size check above the context creation. Replace lines 680-688 with: compute `CGFloat barW = 2, gap = 1; NSUInteger bars = (NSUInteger)(size.width / (barW + gap)); if (bars == 0 || size.width <= 0 || size.height <= 0) return nil;` FIRST, then call UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions(size, NO, 0) and take ctx. Keep the single UIGraphicsEndImageContext() at line 716.

what: +iconNamed:draw: always paints the glyph in opaque black — `CGContextSetRGBFillColor(ctx, 0, 0, 0, 1); CGContextSetRGBStrokeColor(ctx, 0, 0, 0, 1);` — and relies on template rendering to recolour it: `if ([image respondsToSelector:@selector(imageWithRenderingMode:)]) image = [image imageWithRenderingMode:UIImageRenderingModeAlwaysTemplate];` (line 80). imageWithRenderingMode: does not exist on iOS 6, and neither does UIView.tintColor (see src/UIView+SafeTint.m, whose whole job is to swallow that setter).
failure: On the target device (iPhone 4S, iOS 6.1.3) the respondsToSelector: check is always NO, so every TGIcons glyph is a hard black bitmap that nothing can recolour. Select the Dark theme (TGThemeStyleDark is offered in Settings on iOS 6) and: the composer buttons — [TGIcons attach] at src/TGChatViewController.m:1545, [TGIcons sticker] at 1621, [TGIcons microphone] at 1651 — are black glyphs on the #202020 input bar returned by -inputBarColour, i.e. invisible; and the settings list glyphs at src/TGSettingsViewController.m:1164-1165 (`cell.imageView.image = [TGIcons menuGlyphNamed:row[1]]; [cell.imageView tg_setTintColor:[theme secondaryTextColour]];`) are black on the #212121 -listBackgroundColour, also invisible, because tg_setTintColor: is a no-op on iOS 6.
fix: Make the glyph colour part of the drawing rather than a post-hoc tint. In +iconNamed:draw: replace the hardcoded black at lines 72-73 with the theme's glyph colour (e.g. `UIColor *ink = [TGTheme shared].isDark ? [UIColor whiteColor] : [UIColor blackColor];` set via CGContextSetFillColorWithColor/CGContextSetStrokeColorWithColor), and extend the cache key on line 52 to include the dark flag — today it is only `[NSString stringWithFormat:@"%@-%d", name, (int)flat]` and isFlat is YES for both Flat and Dark, so Flat and Dark would collide on the same cache entry. Keep the imageWithRenderingMode: call for iOS 7+ hosts. [TGIcons flush] is already wired to the theme-changed notification (src/TGChatListViewController.m:977, src/TGChatViewController.m:1435).

what: Seven palette accessors branch on -isDarkStyle, which is defined at line 136 as `return _style == TGThemeStyleDark && _imported == nil;` — i.e. deliberately false whenever a theme file is loaded. -fileTileColour (369), -fileMetaColour (382), -mutedBadgeColour (399), -serviceBubbleColour (422), -serviceTextColour (427), -bubbleBorderColour (304) and -separatorColour (414) therefore always take their light-theme branch under an imported theme, even one that declares itself dark (TGThemeFile writes palette[@"isDark"] = @YES, and -isDark at line 93 honours it).
failure: Import any dark .attheme/.tgios-theme: the chat renders with dark bubbles and dark list background, but every document/file block still gets the near-white #EBF0F4 tile from TG_FILE_TILE and #A1AAB3 meta text, and -bubbleBorderColour returns black at 12% — which -separatorColour then reuses for every hairline — so table separators and bubble outlines are invisible black-on-black. Only the six colours the file happens to define are dark; the rest of the UI stays light, producing white tiles punched into a dark chat.
fix: Gate these seven on -isDark rather than -isDarkStyle. -isDarkStyle should remain only where the built-in dark defaults must not override a file's own colour (i.e. inside accessors that first consult -importedColour: and fall through). Concretely change lines 304, 369, 382, 399, 414, 422 and 427 from `self.isDarkStyle` to `self.isDark`.

what: +avatarWithInitials:size:colourId: (849), TGGlyphAvatar (781, behind +archiveAvatarOfSide:/+savedMessagesAvatarOfSide:/+inviteFriendsAvatarOfSide:), +mediaDiscOfSide:playing: (589), +fileDiscOfSide: (616), +callArrowOutgoing:missed: (269), +bubbleTailForColour:outgoing: (720) and +ticksWhite: (746) each open a fresh bitmap context, draw, and return a brand-new UIImage on every call. Only +iconNamed:draw: uses sCache; none of these do.
failure: They are called straight out of cell configuration: src/TGChatListViewController.m:1386/2375/2438, src/TGContactsViewController.m:1292/1371, src/TGChatViewController.m:4699/4756/4878/4997/5035, src/TGSearchViewController.m:1831/1894. Scrolling the chat list on the 4S allocates a new CGBitmapContext plus a CGImage per row per reuse — a 40pt avatar at scale 2 is 40*40*4*4 = 25.6KB, and TGGlyphAvatar additionally builds a CGGradient each time. At ~10 visible rows and continuous scrolling this is megabytes of short-lived allocations per second against a 40-60MB budget, and the drawing itself runs synchronously on the main thread inside tableView:cellForRowAtIndexPath:, which is the scroll stutter.
fix: Give these the same treatment +iconNamed:draw: already has: an NSMutableDictionary (or NSCache) keyed by the arguments that affect the pixels — for avatars `[NSString stringWithFormat:@"av-%@-%.0f-%lld-%d", initials, size, colourId, (int)[TGTheme shared].isFlat]`, for the discs/tail/ticks the side plus colour plus flags. Clear it from +flush, which is already invoked on TGThemeChangedNotification.

what: The avatar colour mapping `static const NSUInteger order[7] = {0, 7, 4, 1, 6, 3, 5}; NSArray *c = palette[order[(NSUInteger)llabs(colourId) % 7]];` indexes an 8-entry palette whose 8th entry is declared as `@[@0.882f, @0.443f, @0.463f]  // the 8th slot repeats red` — the same values as entry 0.
failure: order never contains 2, so the violet colour at palette[2] is unreachable: no user or chat is ever drawn violet. And because order[0]=0 and order[1]=7 both resolve to the identical red, users with colourId%7==0 and colourId%7==1 get the same avatar colour — roughly 2/7 of placeholders are red and the set of distinct colours is six, not seven, so avatar colours do not match what other Telegram clients show for the same person.
fix: Either drop the duplicate 8th entry and use `palette[(NSUInteger)llabs(colourId) % 7]` directly, or correct the order table so it is a permutation of 0..6 that includes 2.

what: -badgeColour (393), -mutedBadgeColour (398) and -profileHeaderColour (353) are declared in TGTheme.h (lines 90, 91, 78) and implemented, but grep over every other .m file in src/ returns zero call sites for all three.
failure: No runtime failure — but the unread badge and profile header are being coloured by hand somewhere else, so an imported theme's accent colour never reaches them while these accessors sit unused and give the false impression that it does. Any future fix applied here would have no effect.
fix: Either delete the three accessors and their header declarations, or wire them up: the chat-list unread badge should take -badgeColour / -mutedBadgeColour and the profile header block -profileHeaderColour, which is what their header comments claim.

what: `+ (NSUInteger)memoryMB { return (NSUInteger)([NSProcessInfo processInfo].physicalMemory / (1024 * 1024)); }` duplicates +[TGDevice memoryMB] (src/TGDevice.m:106), which answers from the hardware table and only falls back to physicalMemory for unknown models. Nothing calls the TGCapabilities version — the one call site, src/TGDeviceViewController.m:77, uses [TGDevice memoryMB].
failure: Dead duplicate, and the two disagree: physicalMemory on a 512MB iPhone 4S reports 512 or less after the kernel's reservation, while the table says 512 exactly. If anyone later calls the TGCapabilities copy to reproduce a tier decision they will get a different tier than +[TGDevice tier], whose armv7 branch is `[self memoryMB] > 512 ? Legacy : Vintage` (TGDevice.m:127) — a strict > against a value that may round down.
fix: Delete +[TGCapabilities memoryMB] and its declaration in TGCapabilities.h line 28; callers should use +[TGDevice memoryMB].

what: The header documents contracts the implementation does not honour: `- (CGFloat)bubbleBorderWidth;  ///< 0 when flat` but TGTheme.m:436 returns a flat 1.0f unconditionally, and `- (UIColor *)bubbleBorderColour;  ///< clear when flat` (TGTheme.h:70) but TGTheme.m:298-307 returns black at 12% alpha for the flat style too. Separately, TGCapabilities.h:45 documents video calls as starting at the A7 while TGCapabilities.m:48 requires TGDeviceTierFull (A9 / 2GB).
failure: A caller that reads the header and skips the border draw when flat, or that trusts a width of 0 to mean 'no hairline', gets a 1pt black hairline it did not expect — the flat/iOS-7 bubble picks up an outline the design does not have. No crash, but the two files disagree about the same contract, so whichever one a future edit trusts is wrong.
fix: Pick one. The implementation is the intended behaviour per the comment at TGTheme.m:299-303 ('their bubbles carry a hairline whatever the era'), so correct the header comments on TGTheme.h:70 and 102 to say the hairline is always drawn, and change TGCapabilities.h:45 to say A9/Full to match the code.

what: The disk cache validity check compares a POINT size against a PIXEL size, so it rejects every cached file it ever wrote: `if (cached && (fabs(cached.size.width - side) > 0.5f || fabs(cached.size.height - side) > 0.5f)) cached = nil;`
failure: TGMediaViewController.m:452 calls `loadWithFileId:... square:TGMediaTileSide * scale` = 75*2 = 150, so `side` is 150 pixels. TGDecodeSquareThumbnail (src/TGImageDecode.m:29) builds the thumb with `UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions(CGSizeMake(side, side), NO, 0)` - scale 0 means screen scale, i.e. 2 on the 4S - producing a UIImage of size 150x150 POINTS backed by 300x300 PIXELS. Line 149-151 writes that as `<fileId>_150.png`, a 300x300 pixel file. On the next appearance line 128 does `[UIImage imageWithContentsOfFile:cachePath]`; the filename has no `@2x` suffix so the image comes back with scale 1.0 and size 300x300 points. `fabs(300 - 150) = 150 > 0.5` -> `cached = nil`. The disk cache therefore has a 100% miss rate: every media tile re-issues a TDLib downloadFile, re-decodes, re-encodes a PNG and rewrites the identical file on every single scroll pass, forever, and the Caches directory grows without ever being read.
fix: Compare in pixels, not points. Replace line 129 with `if (cached && (fabs(cached.size.width * cached.scale - side) > 0.5f || fabs(cached.size.height * cached.scale - side) > 0.5f)) cached = nil;`. Separately fix the double-scaling: `side` is already in pixels at the call site, so TGDecodeSquareThumbnail must not multiply by the screen scale again - pass 1.0f instead of 0 as the scale argument of UIGraphicsBeginImageContextWithOptions in src/TGImageDecode.m:29, and after `[UIImage imageWithContentsOfFile:]` re-wrap with `[UIImage imageWithCGImage:cached.CGImage scale:[UIScreen mainScreen].scale orientation:UIImageOrientationUp]` so the tile draws at the right size.

what: The shared thumbnail NSCache is bounded by object COUNT, not bytes: `cache.countLimit = 96;` while the objects it holds are 300x300-pixel decoded UIImages.
failure: Because of the double-scaling described in the previous finding, each cached media thumbnail is 300x300 RGBA = 360 KB resident (the tile only ever displays 75x75 points, i.e. 150x150 pixels, so 4x more than needed). 96 entries x 360 KB = ~34 MB of decoded bitmaps in a process whose total usable footprint on a 512 MB iPhone 4S is roughly 40-60 MB. Scrolling a chat's shared-media grid past ~96 tiles reaches that ceiling and the app is jetsammed by iOS 6 before the memory-warning observer at line 17-22 (which only fires on a warning, and only after the allocation already happened) can help.
fix: Switch to a cost-based bound: drop `countLimit` and set `cache.totalCostLimit = 3 * 1024 * 1024;`, then pass the byte cost at both insertion sites (line 133 and line 152) with `[TGRemoteImageMemoryCache() setObject:img forKey:cacheKey cost:(NSUInteger)(CGImageGetHeight(img.CGImage) * CGImageGetBytesPerRow(img.CGImage))]`. Also decode at the real display size (see the TGImageDecode scale fix above) so each entry is 150x150 pixels / 90 KB rather than 360 KB.

what: `NSString *cachePath = [self cachePathForKey:cacheKey];` runs on the main thread, and `cachePathForKey:` (lines 70-77) performs a filesystem mutation on every call: `[[NSFileManager defaultManager] createDirectoryAtPath:dir withIntermediateDirectories:YES attributes:nil error:nil]`.
failure: `loadWithFileId:square:placeholder:forceFade:` is called once per tile from TGMediaGridCell.configureWithItems: inside -tableView:cellForRowAtIndexPath:, i.e. 4 times per row on the main thread while the grid is scrolling. Each call issues NSSearchPathForDirectoriesInDomains plus a mkdir syscall against the app container. On an iPhone 4S that is several milliseconds of blocking I/O per row, which shows up directly as dropped frames and jerky scrolling in Shared Media.
fix: Hoist the directory creation out of the per-call path: add a `static NSString *TGRemoteImageCacheDir(void)` that resolves the Caches path and calls createDirectoryAtPath: inside a `dispatch_once`, and make `cachePathForKey:` a pure `[TGRemoteImageCacheDir() stringByAppendingPathComponent:[key stringByAppendingString:@".png"]]` with no FileManager call.

what: The URL-loading API declared in the header is a silent no-op: `- (void)loadImage:(NSString *)__unused url filter:(NSString *)__unused filter placeholder:(UIImage *)placeholder forceFade:(bool)__unused forceFade { self.placeholderImage = placeholder; self.image = placeholder; }`. The companion `currentUrl` property (TGRemoteImageView.h:10) is never written or read anywhere in the tree, and `-tryFillCache:` (line 52) has no callers.
failure: TGRemoteImageView.h:15-16 advertise `loadImage:filter:placeholder:` and its forceFade variant as image loaders. Any future caller that uses the header as written gets a view permanently stuck on the placeholder with no error, no callback and no way to tell loading failed - the exact class of bug that costs an hour to find because the method visibly exists and visibly runs. Only `loadWithFileId:square:placeholder:forceFade:` actually loads anything.
fix: Delete both `loadImage:filter:placeholder:` overloads (lines 61-68) and their header declarations (TGRemoteImageView.h:15-16), delete the unused `currentUrl` property (TGRemoteImageView.h:10), and delete `-tryFillCache:` (lines 52-59) plus its declaration (TGRemoteImageView.h:13). If a URL loader is wanted later, add it then with a real implementation.

what: The recognizer defaults to accepting both directions - `self.direction = TGSwipeGestureRecognizerDirectionLeft | TGSwipeGestureRecognizerDirectionRight;` - and the only call site, TGChatListViewController.m:220-222, never narrows it: `TGSwipeGestureRecognizer *swipe = [[TGSwipeGestureRecognizer alloc] initWithTarget:self action:@selector(swipeRecognised:)]; [self addGestureRecognizer:swipe];`
failure: The chat-list swipe actions are a right-anchored panel: TGChatListViewController.m:layoutSwipeButtonsCollapsed lays the buttons out from `width - kSwipeEdgeDistance` leftwards and animates them in from the right edge. Because the recognizer accepts a rightward swipe too, dragging a chat row to the RIGHT (the natural gesture for 'go back' / 'dismiss') pops open the Delete/Mute panel from the opposite edge. On a delete-capable row that is one mis-swipe away from destructive UI appearing where the user did not ask for it.
fix: At TGChatListViewController.m:220, after allocating the recognizer, add `swipe.direction = TGSwipeGestureRecognizerDirectionLeft;` before `[self addGestureRecognizer:swipe];`.

what: Six classes in this area are compiled into the binary (Makefile lines 231-237) but are never referenced from any other translation unit: TGActionTableView (257 lines), TGLabel (101), TGDateLabel (138), TGHighlightImageView (17), TGHighlightTriggerLabel (16), and the concrete TGReusableView base class (11). A whole-tree grep for each class name outside its own .m/.h pair returns only the TGReusableView *protocol* adoptions and the `prepareForRecycle:(TGViewRecycler *)` signature - no `alloc`, no `[[TGActionTableView` , no `[[TGDateLabel`, no `[[TGLabel`, no `[[TGHighlight...`.
failure: About 540 lines of Objective-C plus their metadata, method lists and selector strings are linked into an app running on a 512 MB device, and every future agent reading the tree has to work out whether TGLabel or plain UILabel is 'the' label class and whether TGActionTableView is the table the chat list uses (it is not - TGChatListViewController uses a plain UITableView). The TGViewRecycler API `-recycledCount:` (TGViewRecycler.m:79) is likewise never called.
fix: Drop `src/TGActionTableView.m`, `src/TGLabel.m`, `src/TGDateLabel.m`, `src/TGHighlightImageView.m`, `src/TGHighlightTriggerLabel.m` and `src/TGReusableView.m` from APP_SRC_M in the Makefile (lines 231-237) and delete the files together with their headers; keep only `TGReusableView.h`'s *protocol* declaration, which TGViewRecycler, TGRemoteImageView and TGStickerTile do use, by moving the `@protocol TGReusableView` block into TGViewRecycler.h and deleting the `@interface TGReusableView : UIView` class. Also delete `-recycledCount:` from TGViewRecycler.h:9 and .m:79-85.

what: The duplicate guard returns before the cleanup work: `if ([views indexOfObjectIdenticalTo:view] != NSNotFound) return;` sits at line 65, ahead of `[view prepareForRecycle:self]` (line 68) and `[view removeFromSuperview]` (line 70-71).
failure: If the same view is handed to -recycleView: twice (it is already sitting in the pool), the second call leaves it installed in its superview and still holding its content/targets while it is simultaneously advertised as free. A later -dequeueReusableViewWithIdentifier: hands that still-parented view to a different cell, which re-parents it, silently blanking the region of the first cell. The original 2013 recycler (TelegraphKit/TGViewRecycler.m:51-73) had no such guard at all and always ran prepareForRecycle first; this reordering is a local regression, currently unreachable only because both call sites (TGStickerPanelView.m:752/816 and TGMediaViewController.m:416/440) clear their tracking collection right after recycling.
fix: Move `[view prepareForRecycle:self]` and the `removeFromSuperview` block above the `indexOfObjectIdenticalTo:` check so the view is always detached and reset, and let the duplicate check only skip the final `[views addObject:view]`.

what: `- (void)cancelLoading { self.cancelled = true; }` latches the flag permanently, and only `loadWithFileId:square:placeholder:forceFade:` (line 95) ever clears it - `prepareForReuse` (line 38), `prepareForRecycle:` (line 45) and `loadPlaceholder:` (line 161) all set it and never reset.
failure: Any code path that calls -loadPlaceholder: (or the stub -loadImage:...) and then expects a later in-flight delivery to land gets nothing: the `me.cancelled` test in the `deliver` block at line 120 short-circuits forever. Today this is latent because the media grid always goes through loadWithFileId:, but the header exposes cancelLoading/loadPlaceholder as public API with no documented one-shot semantics.
fix: Set `self.cancelled = false;` at the top of `-loadPlaceholder:` (after the cancelLoading call, line 161) and at the top of `-loadImage:filter:placeholder:forceFade:` if that method is kept, so `cancelled` is strictly per-load rather than per-lifetime.

what: `[(id<TGAdvancedHighlightable>)target advancedSetHighlighted:highlighted];` casts an element of the untyped `targetViews` array to a protocol it was never checked against - the array is `@property (nonatomic, strong) NSArray *targetViews;` with no element type and no respondsToSelector: guard.
failure: With `advanced == true`, any target in the array that implements only the required `TGHighlightable` -setHighlighted: (which is what every plain UIImageView/UILabel provides) raises `-[UIImageView advancedSetHighlighted:]: unrecognized selector sent to instance` and terminates the app the moment the row is touched. The class is currently uninstantiated so this is unreachable today, but it will fire the first time anyone wires it up with a mixed target array.
fix: If the class is kept rather than deleted per the dead-code finding, guard the branch: `if (self.advanced && [target respondsToSelector:@selector(advancedSetHighlighted:)]) [(id<TGAdvancedHighlightable>)target advancedSetHighlighted:highlighted]; else [target setHighlighted:highlighted];`. Also call `[super setHighlighted:highlighted]` first - the current override swallows it, so the label's own highlightedTextColor never takes effect.

what: Every cache-hit delivery runs a snapshot-based cross-dissolve: `[UIView transitionWithView:self duration:duration options:UIViewAnimationOptionTransitionCrossDissolve animations:^{ self.image = image; } completion:nil];`, and TGMediaTileView sets `self.fadeTransition = true` (TGMediaViewController.m:299) so `fade` is true for every tile.
failure: UIViewAnimationOptionTransitionCrossDissolve makes UIKit render two offscreen snapshots of the view and blend them for the duration. During a Shared Media scroll, four tiles per row each start their own transition as their thumbnail arrives, so the single A5 core is compositing 8 extra offscreen surfaces per row on top of the decode work - measurable stutter on a 4S for a 0.14s effect nobody sees while scrolling.
fix: Only fade when the view is not being filled during active scrolling: skip the transition when the previous contents were already a real image, e.g. `if (fade && self.image == self.placeholderImage) { ...transition... } else { self.image = image; }`, or expose a `suppressFade` flag that TGMediaViewController sets while `tableView.isDragging || tableView.isDecelerating`.

what: -sendChecks bails out on `if (!self.peerPwd.length || self.socketHandle < 0) return;`, but in reflector (transport) mode -start returns at line 38 before any socket is created, so _socketHandle stays -1 forever and the `if (self.transport) { self.transport(request); return; }` branch at lines 101-104 is unreachable dead code.
failure: Every real call on this build uses the reflector transport (TGCall.mm:184 sets ice.transport). The 0.3s checker timer fires, hits the socketHandle guard and returns, so the client never emits a single STUN binding request. Only the peer's inbound checks are answered; our side never nominates a pair, the peer's ICE agent never sees a check from us, and the call sits in TGCallStateConnecting until the peer discards it.
fix: In -sendChecks change the guard to `if (!self.peerPwd.length) return; if (!self.transport && self.socketHandle < 0) return;` so the transport branch at line 101 is reached. The socket guard must apply only to the direct-socket path below line 106.

what: -teardown clears ice/reflectors/controller but never resets the signalling state it set up: `sentCandidates`, `callKey`, `signallingSeq`, `currentSenderTag`, `currentReflector`, `peerUfrag`, `peerPwd`, `localUfrag`, `localPwd`, `reflectorHost`. `sentCandidates` is a one-way latch, and -sendOurCandidates starts with `if (self.sentCandidates || !self.reflectorHost.length) return;` (line 173).
failure: TGCall is a process-wide singleton (+shared). The first call sets sentCandidates=YES. Every subsequent call in the same app run reaches -probeReflectorsIn:key: -> -sendOurCandidates, returns immediately, and so never creates a TGCallIce, never sends its candidates message and never learns the peer's ufrag/pwd. The second and all later calls hang in Connecting and are discarded. Stale callKey also means signalling from the new call is decrypted with the old key until callStateReady arrives.
fix: At the top of -teardown add: `self.sentCandidates = NO; self.callKey = nil; self.signallingSeq = 0; self.currentSenderTag = 0; self.currentReflector = nil; self.peerUfrag = nil; self.peerPwd = nil; self.localUfrag = nil; self.localPwd = nil; self.reflectorHost = nil; self.reflectorPort = 0;` (before the ice/reflector cleanup).

what: Bounds checks in +parseCandidates use unchecked addition on 32-bit types: `uint32_t size = TGReadU32(bytes + at); at += 4; if (at + size > length) return nil;` (lines 120-123, repeated at 137-140). NSUInteger is 32 bits on armv7, so `at + size` wraps.
failure: A candidates message whose length prefix is e.g. 0xFFFFFFF0 makes `at + size` wrap to a small value, the guard passes, and `[[NSString alloc] initWithBytes:bytes + at length:size ...]` reads ~4GB past the decrypted buffer -> EXC_BAD_ACCESS as soon as it walks off the page. The same happens on the ufrag/pwd loop. The body is peer-controlled (only the call key gates it), so any malformed or truncated candidates message from a modern tgcalls peer kills the app mid-call.
fix: Replace both checks with subtraction that cannot overflow: `if (size > length - at) return nil;` (and `break;` in the credentials loop), keeping the preceding `if (at + 4 > length)` guards rewritten the same way as `if (length < 4 || at > length - 4)`.

what: +wavFromOpusFile: decodes the entire voice note into an in-RAM NSMutableData with `op_read_stereo` at 48 kHz stereo (`const int channels = 2;`, line 39), then builds a second full copy: `NSMutableData *wav = [NSMutableData dataWithBytes:header length:44]; [wav appendData:pcm];` (lines 80-81) before writing it out.
failure: Telegram voice notes are mono. A 60-second note becomes 48000*2*2*60 = 11.5 MB of PCM, plus NSMutableData's doubling reallocs (transient ~23 MB), plus the 11.5 MB `wav` copy, plus the atomic file write buffer: a 30-40 MB peak on a device with 40-60 MB usable. On the 4S, playing a two-minute voice note from a loaded chat screen is a jetsam kill, not a slow decode.
fix: Write the WAV incrementally: open the output with NSFileHandle, write a 44-byte placeholder header, decode with `op_read` (mono, channels = 1) into the stack buffer and `writeData:` each block, then seek to offsets 4 and 40 and patch the RIFF/data sizes. Drop the `pcm` NSMutableData and the `wav` copy entirely; peak RAM becomes the 23 KB stack buffer.

what: -stopRecording has an else branch that ends the recording without ever notifying anyone: `if (self.movieOutput.isRecording) [self.movieOutput stopRecording]; else self.recording = NO;`. -startRecording sets `self.recording = YES` (line 362) synchronously, but AVCaptureMovieFileOutput.isRecording only becomes YES once the output actually starts.
failure: Tap-and-immediately-release the shutter (or an app-background event arriving in the same runloop turn as startRecording): stopRecording sees isRecording == NO, sets recording = NO and returns. -captureOutput:didFinishRecordingToOutputFileAtURL: never fires, so neither videoRecorder:didFinishRecordingToPath:... nor videoRecorder:didFailWithError: reaches TGVideoCaptureViewController - the capture screen stays in its recording UI forever. Worse, the movie output then does start and keeps writing to disk until the 10-minute / 64 MB limit, with nothing left holding the flag that would stop it.
fix: Replace the else branch with a real termination: `else { self.recording = NO; self.discarding ? [self discardOutputFile] : [self failWithCode:TGVideoRecorderErrorTooShort]; self.discarding = NO; }` - or better, keep a `stopRequested` flag and call -stopRecording again from -captureOutput:didStartRecordingToOutputFileAtURL: so the pending stop is honoured once the output is really running.

what: callStateReady is read straight out of the TDLib dictionary with no type guards: `NSData *key = [[NSData alloc] initWithBase64EncodedString:state[@"encryption_key"] options:0];`, and the same for `type[@"peer_tag"]` (line 451, 518) and `server[@"ip_address"]` (line 521).
failure: If encryption_key is absent or is not a string (any TDLib schema drift, or a reply this build's schema does not match), -initWithBase64EncodedString:options: is handed nil/an NSNumber and raises NSInvalidArgumentException on iOS 6 - an uncaught crash on the main queue the moment a call reaches Ready. TGCallReflector -initWithHost: with a non-NSString host later crashes in -UTF8String at TGCallReflector.m:59.
fix: Before line 433 add `NSString *encoded = [state[@"encryption_key"] isKindOfClass:NSString.class] ? state[@"encryption_key"] : nil; if (!encoded) { self.state = TGCallStateFailed; return; }` and use `encoded`. Guard `type[@"peer_tag"]` and `server[@"ip_address"]` with the same isKindOfClass:NSString.class check, skipping the server when either fails.

what: -inspectReflectorPacket: dereferences the first four bytes with no length check: `if (packet.length <= 32){ NSLog(@"... first %02x%02x%02x%02x", ..., bytes[0], bytes[1], bytes[2], bytes[3]); return; }`. The only guard above it is that the packet is <= 32 bytes.
failure: TGCallReflector -readLoop (TGCallReflector.m:164-181) forwards every datagram with `got > 0`, including 1-3 byte packets. A short/garbage UDP datagram from the reflector (or any host that guesses the ephemeral port) reads up to 3 bytes past the NSData allocation; on a page boundary that is an EXC_BAD_ACCESS during an active call.
fix: Change the guard to `if (packet.length < 4){ NSLog(@"TGCall: %lu-byte reflector packet", (unsigned long)packet.length); return; } if (packet.length <= 32){ ...existing log... }`.

what: -sendMedia: and the `onMedia` block property are never used anywhere in the tree: `onMedia` is only ever read at TGCallIce.m:151 and 176 and is never assigned (TGCall.mm sets only `transport` and `onConnected`), and -sendMedia: has no callers. TGCallMessages.h:16-17 `TGCallMessageMediaState`/`TGCallMessageAudioData` are declared and defined but never referenced either.
failure: No runtime failure - but the media path looks wired up when reading TGCallIce.h, which is how the reflector-mode ICE work above got left half-finished. Anyone tracing why no audio flows will follow onMedia and find nothing on the other end.
fix: Either delete -sendMedia:, the `onMedia` property and its two call sites plus the two unused message-type constants, or wire onMedia in TGCall.mm -sendOurCandidates alongside `transport`/`onConnected` and feed it into the audio path. Do not leave it declared and unassigned.

what: Three private properties are written but never read: `reflectorPort` (written at line 538), `reflectorId` (written at line 539, and its value comes from the already-incremented `index` inside the NSLog on line 532), and `loggedHeader` (declared line 124, never written or read at all).
failure: No runtime failure; each is 4-8 bytes of a singleton. They are leftovers from an earlier single-reflector design and make -probeReflectorsIn:key: look like it maintains state that later code depends on.
fix: Delete the three @property lines (120, 121, 124) and the two assignments at lines 538-539.

what: The decoded WAV always lands on one fixed path: `NSString *out = [NSTemporaryDirectory() stringByAppendingPathComponent:@"voice.wav"];`, unlike TGVoiceRecorder which uses a timestamp+random name (TGVoiceRecorder.m:33-37).
failure: Decoding runs on a global queue (TGChatViewController.m:3928). Tap voice note A, then B before A's AVAudioPlayer has been created: B's decode overwrites voice.wav, and the main-queue block for A then builds its player from B's file - the user hears the wrong voice note. The file also never gets deleted, so temp holds one stale multi-MB WAV indefinitely.
fix: Name the output after the source, e.g. `[NSString stringWithFormat:@"voice-%@.wav", opusPath.lastPathComponent]`, and have TGChatViewController remove the previous WAV in -stopPlayback.
